destinations.name: Johor Bahru
destinations.intro: Johor Bahru (Jawi: جوهر بهرو, Chinese: 新山) (also Johor Baru or Johore Baharu, or just JB) is Malaysia's second largest city, and the state capital of Johor. The city is surrounded by suburbs, industrial parks and long waterfront areas, in the southern part of Peninsular Malaysia.
destinations.eat_notes: Johor Bahru offers local delicacies of Malaysia to Western and Asian choices of food. Dining venues range from budget and mid-range eateries to high-end restaurants with various price ranges. Many of them are in restaurant and entertainment districts, shopping malls, along sea fronts, hawker centres, pedestrian zones, food courts, stand alone food stalls or even food trucks.

notes.title: School holidays
notes.text: Late May to June and most of December are school holidays: book early, and expect traffic and queues at anything family-friendly.

notes.title: Hari Raya Aidilfitri
notes.text: The biggest holiday of the year. Cities empty out, highways jam with people heading home, and many eateries close for the first few days. The date moves about 11 days earlier every year.

notes.title: Chinese New Year
notes.text: Lanterns, lion dances and open houses. Many Chinese-run shops and eateries close for the first two or three days, so plan your meals.

places.name: Chinatown
places.text: This historical Chinese community area is located mostly along the Tan Hiok Nee Street.

places.name: Little India
places.text: This historical Indian community area is located mostly along the Ungku Puan Street.

places.name: Majidee Malay Village
places.text: This Malay community area is located mostly along the Masjid Street. It consists of various restaurants, shops and landmarks, such as Majidee Malay Village Market and Majidee Malay Village Jamek Mosque.

places.name: JLand Tower
places.text: An iconic skyscraper with lightshow on its outer glass windows at night. It has a gallery and viewing platform at its 34th level to see the skyline of Johor Bahru named Skyscape.

places.name: Johor Bahru City Square
places.text: Johor Bahru City Square is a public square that was constructed in conjunction with Johor Bahru being granted city status on January 1994. A grey-coloured building with a gigantic clock tower built stands on the north edge of the square.

places.name: Johor Public Library
places.text: The main public library of Johor Bahru. It also consists the Petrosains PlaySmart Johor Bahru science centre.

places.name: Mahmoodiah Royal Mausoleum
places.text: This is a royal mausoleum of Johor state. The first sultan of Johor laid to rest here was Sultan Abu Bakar in 1895, as are the three sultans that reigned after him: Ibrahim, Ismail and Iskandar.

places.name: Permaisuri Zarith Sofiah Opera House
places.text: Performing arts theater with modern architecture design facing the Tebrau Strait.
places.address: Mercu 2, Jalan Tanjung Puteri 1, R&F Puteri, 80300

places.name: Permas Square
places.text: An open space square which also consists of football field, hockey field, children playground and roof-covered futsal field.

places.name: Persada Johor International Convention Centre
places.text: Convention centre designed with an architecture that resembles the official hat of Johor Sultanate.

places.name: Serene Square
places.text: This is a public square in front of Serene Palace. It features a 12-m-high star and crescent statue. The ground features a double 5-corner star, which makes it in total of 10, representing the total numbers of districts in Johor.

places.name: Sultan Ismail Library
places.text: Public library of the Johor Bahru City Council.

places.name: Tanjung Kupang Memorial Park
places.text: This memorial was erected by the Johor state government in memory of the 100 passengers and crew members killed when Malaysia Airlines Flight 653 (MH653) Boeing 737 crashed at Tanjung Kupang (about 20 km west of Johor Bahru) on the evening of 4 December 1977.

places.name: Arulmigu Rajamariamman Devasthanam Temple
places.text: Free admission for visitors. Everyone has their shoes in the racks beside the gate entrance. The temple also features the Indian Heritage Centre cultural centre.

places.name: Arulmigu Sri Rajakaliamman Glass Temple
places.text: Inaugurated in 1996 and touted as "The First Glass Temple in the World". The inner surface of the walls and the columns inside the temple are clad with imported glass, hence the name.

places.name: Church of the Immaculate Conception
places.text: Beige building with a single steeple (with spire) is one of the main Roman Catholic churches in Johor Bahru. Built in 1883 in the British colonial style, it is one of the oldest structures still standing in Johor Bahru.

places.name: Gurdwara Sahib Johor Bahru
places.text: This Sikh temple was built on the site of the smaller and older Sikh temple and was inaugurated on 28 August 1992. This is a 2-storey white building with yellow window frames and an all-round, crenellated roof parapet.

places.name: India Mosque
places.text: This mosque has two different minarets and was founded by the city's Indian Muslim community. It is a modern-looking mosque with white walls, blue-tinted glass cladding on both its minarets and a blue and silver dome.

places.name: Johor Bahru Old Chinese Temple
places.text: It is a Chinese temple believed to be built in 1870 by a group of Chinese community leaders led by Tan Hiok Nee, a famous, local Teochew businessman.

places.name: Sultan Abu Bakar State Mosque
places.text: Located on top of a small hill and overlooking the Straits of Johor, this state mosque took eight years to construct (1892-1900). It has four minarets that resemble British clock towers.

places.name: Sultan Iskandar Mosque
places.text: Built in 2013, the mosque has been declared as Malaysia's first tourism-friendly mosque after the Malaysia Tourism Quality Assurance certificate issued by the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture.
places.address: No. 2, Jalan Dato' Onn 2, Bandar Dato Onn, 81100

places.name: Royal Abu Bakar Museum
places.text: The Royal Abu Bakar Museum is one of the oldest buildings in Johor and is one of the main attractions in the state. This building was built in the year of 1866.

places.name: Figure Museum
places.text: The museum is housed in a building constructed in 1893 which was once used as the official residence of the first Chief Minister of Johor. As of July 2024, it is under renovation with an unknown date to reopen.

places.name: Johor Bahru Chinese Heritage Museum
places.text: Housed in a restored 4-storey building. Learn about the history and culture of the Chinese community in Johor Bahru. The displays are spread out over four storeys.

places.name: Johor Bahru Hokkien Association Museum
places.text: The museum showcases the important historical events, such as Malaya during World War 2, cultural relics and the historical development of Fujian.
places.address: Hokkien Building, No. 2D, Jalan Yahya Awal, Kampung Kertak Merah, 80000

places.name: KTM Museum
places.text: The museum used to be the main railway station of Johor Bahru.

places.name: Museum of 24 Festive Drum
places.text: Museum about Chinese drums, located above a cafe.

places.name: Glulam Gallery
places.text: It is a gallery which was opened on 22 May 2012.

places.name: Johor Bahru Kwong Siew Heritage Gallery
places.text: Museum occupies 2 units of adjoining 2-storey shop houses that were completed in 1907.

places.name: Johor Craft Complex
places.text: Contains a so-called Treasured Possession Gallery exhibits batik, embroidery and beads. It also hosts a handicrafts fair on its premises once a year.

places.name: Johor Heritage Foundation

places.name: Johor Japan Football Gallery

destinations.name: Kluang

destinations.name: Muar
destinations.intro: Muar is the second biggest town and district of the state of Johor, at its northeast, in southern Peninsular Malaysia. Muar is also known by its other name, Bandar Maharani, which means Empress Town. It is the de jure royal capital of Johor, and the Sultan of Johor maintains a palace in the town, though in practice he spends most of his time in Johor Bahru.
destinations.eat_notes: Local delicious Malay foods like mee bandung, rojak petis, satay Muar and asam pedas are the signature foods of Muar. Don't forget delicious Javanese foods like soto, mee rebus, lontong and nasi ambeng. Locals are famous for eating pisang goreng (fried banana) and tempe goreng (fried Javanese fermented soya bean cake) with a dip of thick soya sauce with hot chili.

destinations.intro: Kota Tinggi is a town in Kota Tinggi District, Johor, Malaysia. Kota Tinggi is known as a historical town because the Sultanate of Johor was established there. Many historical tombs are found here including the Sultan Mahmud Mangkat Di Julang Mausoleum, Makam Bendahara Tun Habib Abdul Majid and Makam Tauhid in Kampung Makam.

destinations.name: Langkawi
destinations.intro: Langkawi (Jawi: لانكاوي), officially known as "Langkawi, the Jewel of Kedah" (Malay: Langkawi Permata Kedah) is an archipelago of 99 islands (an extra 5 temporary islands are revealed at low tide) in the Andaman Sea, 30 km off the mainland coast of Kedah.
destinations.eat_notes: There are food stalls and restaurants all over Langkawi. Try one of the many seafood restaurants. Langkawi people like their food hot and spicy, and even if they tone things down at your request, you may still find your food challenging to eat.

destinations.name: Kulim
destinations.intro: Kulim is a city of 272,000 people (2010) in Kedah. Bordering Penang in the west, Kulim is an ever-developing district where the Kulim Hi-Tech Park, the first high technology industrial park in Malaysia that was established in 1996, is situated.
destinations.eat_notes: Kulim's cuisine reflects the Chinese, Nyonya, Malay and Indian ethnic mix of Malaysia due to directly influence by Penang state (the food capital of Malaysia), but also shows some influence of Thailand.

notes.title: School holidays
notes.text: Late May to June and most of December are school holidays: book early, and expect traffic and queues at anything family-friendly.

notes.title: Hari Raya Aidilfitri
notes.text: The biggest holiday of the year. Cities empty out, highways jam with people heading home, and many eateries close for the first few days. The date moves about 11 days earlier every year.

places.name: Kulim Hi-Tech Park
places.text: 8 km from Kulim Town. It was the first integrated Hi-tech Park in Malaysia. The main activities at this park are jogging and cycling whilst enjoying the breathtaking wonders of the landscape.

places.name: Sungai Sedim Recreational Forest
places.text: Sungai Sedim with its fast currents and rapids along with a forest ecosystem is the best place for exciting recreational activities. The main activities here include kayaking and white water rafting.

places.name: Ulu Paip RainForest
places.text: In the Forest Reserves of Mount Bungsu with rapid river and forest ecosystem surroundings. The main activities here include picnicking, dipping, swimming and camping.

places.name: Kulim Lake Garden
places.text: Putra Lake is the result of tin mining that was carried out in the area, as early as the 1850s. Visitors come here to either jog or take a walk on the pedestrian walk around the lake.

places.name: Paya Besar
places.text: This suburb of Kulim is famously known as the 'Little India of Kulim'. There are many Indian fashion stores here, which sell mostly sarees, silk and cotton, almost anything that has the essence of India.

places.name: Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
places.text: Famous and biggest Roman Catholic parish church in Kulim. The church in was established in 1948.

places.name: Merdeka Clock Tower
places.text: The main landmark in Kulim. Ground breaking for the Merdeka Clock Tower was officiated by the late Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra, who was then the Chief Minister of the Federated States of Malaya, on 14 June 1957.

places.name: Nattukkotai Nagaraththar Sri Thandayuthapani Temple
places.text: This is the temple of the Chettiar community in the town. The patron deity of the temple is Murugan, the deity associated with the Hindu festival of Thaipusam.

destinations.eat_notes: Kota Bharu is full of delicious Kelantanese food, a unique cuisine influenced by Thai and Indian styles, among others. Lots of goodies are to be found in the pasars and in coffee shops throughout the city. Chinese food is also available at various restaurants and food courts.

destinations.name: Kuala Lumpur
destinations.intro: Kuala Lumpur, called KL by locals, is Malaysia's federal capital and largest city at 6.5 million (city-proper population of 1.8 million). Kuala Lumpur is a cultural melting pot with some of the world's cheapest 5-star hotels, impressive shopping districts, food from all parts of the world, and natural wonders within day-trip distance.
destinations.eat_notes: Malaysian food is amazing, making Kuala Lumpur an excellent place to eat as it hosts cuisine from all around the country and beyond. Most restaurants close by 10PM, but in the city centre, there are always a few 24-hr kedai mamak (curry houses) or fast food places if you get stuck.

notes.title: School holidays
notes.text: Late May to June and most of December are school holidays: book early, and expect traffic and queues at anything family-friendly.

notes.title: Hari Raya Aidilfitri
notes.text: The biggest holiday of the year. Cities empty out, highways jam with people heading home, and many eateries close for the first few days. The date moves about 11 days earlier every year.

notes.title: Chinese New Year
notes.text: Lanterns, lion dances and open houses. Many Chinese-run shops and eateries close for the first two or three days, so plan your meals.

notes.title: Thaipusam
notes.text: One of the great Hindu processions in the world, at Batu Caves and in George Town. Unforgettable, and extremely crowded.

notes.title: Deepavali
notes.text: Little India streets are lit up and busy with sweets and shopping in the weeks before.

notes.title: Merdeka
notes.text: National Day on 31 August: parades, flags everywhere and road closures in the city centre.

places.name: Batu Caves
places.text: Hindu priests have used these caves as temples since their discovery in 1878 by William Hornaday.

places.name: Badminton
places.text: Built in 1990, the stadium can hold 4,500 spectators.

places.name: ASEAN Sculpture Garden
places.text: A sculpture garden, located next to National Monument in walking distance.

places.name: Dark Caves
places.text: Just off to the side of the entrance to the Batu Caves is the Dark Caves. The Dark Caves is a conservation site showcasing the endemic animals and insects that live in the cave ecosystem.

places.name: Great Eastern Mall
places.text: Great Eastern Mall is adjoined with the Menara Great Eastern and professes to offer a 'fine lifestyle and relaxation' shopping experience.

places.name: Orchid Garden
places.text: The Orchid garden was opened in 1986. 700-800 species of orchids can be seen here. Malaysia has 3000 species altogether. There is a souvenir shop on the premises.

places.name: Muzium Orang Asli
places.text: A quaint museum situated on Orang Asli land that showcases the culture of the different indigenous peoples from Peninsular Malaysia.

places.name: Ampang Point
places.text: Located along Jalan Ampang, this is one of Ampang's main malls and also serves as a RapidKL bus hub.
places.address: Jalan Mamanda 3, Ampang Point, 68000 Ampang, Selangor

places.name: National Palace
places.text: The official residence of the King (Yang Di-Pertuan Agong) of Malaysia. You can get a glance at this gigantic building by going to the main entrance (see geo marker).

places.name: Restaurant Nak Won
places.text: One of popular Korean restaurants in Ampang's Little Korea.
places.address: A11-1-1, Jalan Ampang Utama 2/2, Business Ave, Ampang Jaya

places.name: Hibiscus Garden
places.text: Garden dedicated to the national plant of Malaysia.

places.name: Petronas Twin Towers
places.text: Perhaps the most iconic building of Malaysia and the tallest twin building in the world.
places.address: Jalan Ampang and Jalan P Ramlee

places.name: Kuala Lumpur Courts Complex
places.text: It is said that this Court Complex is the second largest in the world behind the one in India. Although not overly touristy, the arial view of the court resembles a Y-Wing Plane from Star Wars.

places.name: Forest Research Institute of Malaysia (FRIM)
places.text: Guided tours through the rainforest. Includes a canopy walk and a little museum. In 2025 the institute and forest was listed as a .

places.name: Kepong Metropolitan Park
places.text: Located at the northern side of Kepong 6 km from Sri Hartamas, this place features a lake and is ideal for flying kites. Jogging/cycling tracks, remote control car track, football field and observation tower are among the facilities provided.

places.name: Kuala Lumpur Tower
places.text: KL Tower has a viewing deck at 276bm provides great city views, and you'll be a few metres higher than the Twin Towers since the tower is built on a hill (also, the twin towers observation deck is 100 m below at 170 m).

places.name: Federal Territory Mosque
places.text: This large mosque, which was opened in 2000, was partly inspired by the Blue Mosque in Istanbul. The mosque's website is in Malay only.

places.name: Bukit Jalil National Stadium
places.text: Bukit Jalil National Stadium is Malaysia's national stadium, constructed in 1998 to host that year's Commonwealth Games. It was also the venue of the 2001 and 2017 Southeast Asian Games.

places.name: Rama V
places.text: Among the best Thai food in town.

places.name: National Science Centre
places.text: Well done science museum, which is especially great, if you come with children.

places.name: Zouk
places.text: A branch of the famous Singaporean club, opened in 2004. Plays dance/house style music on Friday nights and popular with younger clubbers and rich locals (Ferrari parked outside for show).

places.name: Aquaria KLCC
places.text: A gigantic aquarium housing over 5,000 aquatic and terrestrial species. The aquarium has many displays including an underwater tunnel, interactive touch pools, exhibits of flora and fauna and multimedia kiosks.
places.address: Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre, Jl Pinang

places.name: Swimming classes at the National Aquatic Center
places.text: Olympic size pool. The opening hours are a little weird though: 7 one-hourly sessions on weekdays and 3 evening sessions on the weekends.

places.name: Alexis Bistro & Wine Bar
places.text: Restaurant, which houses live performances - mainly jazz - on almost every weekend. Local and international artists are performing.

places.name: Hiking or mountainbiking in Bukit Kiara
places.text: The most popular spot in the whole city to go mountainbiking or hiking. Unfortunately the forest is constantly reduced in size by greedy building developers.

places.name: Watch an event at Bukit Jalil National Stadium
places.text: This huge stadium with a capacity of 87,411 is used as venue for many sports events and concerts.

places.name: Badan Warisan Malaysia
places.text: A non-profit organisation for the conservation and promotion of Malaysia's heritage and has various exhibits and seminars about Malaysia and its history.

places.name: National Mosque
places.text: Masjid Negara is unique in that it incorporates Malay-Islamic rather than the usual Arabic-Islamic architecture. It is known for its conspicuous turquoise umbrella-like roof.

places.name: The Kuala Lumpur Performing Arts Centre (KLPac)
places.text: Sentul West - KLPac, set up by YTL, one of Malaysia's biggest companies, is a noted centre for performing arts, notably theatre and music (it can also host film screening).

places.name: Heroes' Mausoleum
places.text: The burial ground of several Malaysian leaders and politicians. Construction of the mausoleum began in 1963 under its project of the construction of Masjid Negara and was completed in 1965.

places.name: Petrosains
places.text: An exhibit of the science and technology behind the petroleum industry, mainly aimed for children and sponsored by the Petronas oil company. There are various science shows, interactive exhibits and simulation experiences throughout.

places.name: Reflexology
places.text: Desa Sri Hartamas probably has the largest number of reflexology centres per unit area in KL.

places.name: Endah Parade
places.text: Perhaps the largest mall in the vicinity of the National Stadium. Nothing notable for a tourist, but still convenient for one to get groceries from the AEON BIG hypermarket at the lower-ground floor of this shopping mall.

places.name: Muzium Telekom
places.text: Built in 1928 as the Central Battery Telephone Exchange, converted into the Telecommunications Museum in 1994, showing the growth of communications technology in Malaysia.

places.name: AEON Big Kepong
places.text: Huge supermarket, that has everything you possibly need.
places.address: No.2, Jalan Metro Perdana, Taman Usahawan Kepong

places.name: National Monument
places.text: This immense bronze structure was built as a memorial to the soldiers who gave up their lives for their country.

places.name: Plaza Mont' Kiara Fiesta Nite
places.text: A bazaar every Thursday, selling food, clothing, toys, household appliances, etc.

places.name: The Store Sri Petaling
places.text: Another grocery mart in the vicinity, after Endah Parade. Part of a national chain store. However this mart is located in the more bustling part of Sri Petaling, so to speak.

places.name: Masjid Jamek
places.text: It's at the convergence of the Klang and Gombak rivers. The stately Masjid Jamek, constructed in 1909, is one of the oldest mosques in the city.

places.name: Cheras Leisure Mall
places.text: Easily spotted along the Kuala Lumpur-Kajang-Seremban federal road, this mall, though not as big as Mid Valley, is still the largest neighbourhood mall serving the locals in Cheras.

places.name: Independence Square
places.text: Originally grown by the British as a cricket ground, this square has a special place in the hearts of all Malaysians as it was here that the Union Jack was lowered for last time in 1957 and Malaysia gained her independence.

places.name: Tun Abdul Razak Memorial
places.text: Tun Abdul Razak (11 March 1922 (Pekan) - 14 January 1976 (London)) was the second prime minister of Malaysia. He ruled from 1970 to 1976. He is entombed in Makam Pahlawan.

places.name: Yu Ai Segambut Seafood Noodle
places.text: Truly a local's recommendation. Noodles come with three soup options: their famous curry laksa, tom yam or qingtang (clear soup). Air-cond seating upstairs.

places.name: Eko Cheras Mall
places.text: Located across the KL-Kajang road from Leisure Mall. New mall opened in late-2018, with a grocer store on the ground floor, and the remaining cinema in the area.

places.name: National Museum
places.text: Contains exhibits on traditional life among the various ethnic communities of Malaysia, numerous well-explained artifacts including fine clothing and shadow puppets and Orang Asli woodcarving pieces.

places.name: Sultan Abdul Samad Building
places.text: Fronting the Merdeka Square, the Sultan Abdul Samad Building was built as the offices of the Colonial Secretariat, and later served as the first administrative centre of the Malayan government.

places.name: Berjaya Times Square Theme Park
places.text: Malaysia's largest indoor theme park, located on the upper floors of the giant Berjaya Times Square mall and particularly notable for its hair-raising seven-story indoor roller coaster.

places.name: Kuala Lumpur Railway Station
places.text: A Moorish-style masterpiece designed by Arthur Benison Hubback, a British Architectural Assistant to the Director of Public Works. As well as suburban trains and express trains to Ipoh, it houses a mini-museum of Malaysian railway history.

places.name: Cheras Sentral
places.text: Despite its name, this mall is not a major public transport hub! Only the Kajang Line MRT (metro) and two buses stop here.

places.name: Islamic Arts Museum
places.text: One of the most interesting museums in KL, the Islamic Arts Museum houses both modern and traditional Malaysia as part of the larger Islamic world and, through exhibitions of objects of religious and aesthetic significance, shows both the connection of…

places.name: KL Forest Eco Park
places.text: Being the last virgin tropical rainforest left in Kuala Lumpur, this is certainly not your typical urban park. If lucky you may even be able to spot some wildlife, including birds, monkeys, lizards and even the occasional snake.

places.name: Craft Village @ Kompleks Kraf KL
places.text: Part of a government-owned organisation which was set up to showcase Malaysian art and craft. You can create your own Malay art by having a dabble at batik drawing, wood carving and pottery making, all at a 'minimal fee'.

places.name: Taman Budaya Kuala Lumpur
places.text: It is used as a theatre and arts centre. This building is notable for being the first site of the Victoria Institution until 1929 (refer below). In 1911 it was witness to a sensational murder case - the Ethel Proudlock case.

places.name: National Planetarium
places.text: The attractions here include space science and astronomy exhibits, a theatre screening 3-Dimensional movies, a viewing gallery and an observatory.

places.name: Publika
places.text: Great place with plenty of hip stores. Plenty of food choices and a great supermarket in the basement.

places.name: Taman Connaught night market
places.text: Taman Connaught Chinese pasar malam is the most popular night market in the area, and was dubbed the 'longest Chinese pasar malam in KL'. It's held every Wednesday at the Taman Connaught housing area in Cheras, from dusk until midnight.
places.address: Bus T410 from Taman Connaught metro station in the direction of Bandar Tasik Selatan

places.name: Petronas Philharmonic Hall
places.text: Advance bookings are possible online. Note that a strict dress code applies: long sleeve batik or lounge suit for gala and evening performances, "smart casual" (no jeans, shorts, T-shirts, sneakers and slippers) for other performances.
places.address: Ground Floor, Tower 2, Petronas Twin Towers

places.name: Royal Malaysian Police Museum
places.text: The police museum shows the history of the Malaysian police with pictures, weapons and vehicles.

places.name: Medan Pasar (Market Square) Clock Tower
places.text: Art-Deco clock tower built in 1936/37 to commemorate the coronation of King George VI. The commemorative plague was removed upon Malayan independence in 1957.

places.name: Oriental Building
places.text: Stately Art Deco building towering above the Masjid Jamek metro station. Completed 1933, it was reportedly Kuala Lumpur's tallest structure back then. During the post-war years it was home to Radio Malaya (now Radio Television Malaysia, RTM).

places.name: Malay World Ethnology Museum
places.text: This museum presents the culture of the Malay world (Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines...) especially through its material objects such as brass utensils, weapons, pottery, textiles and musical instruments, as well as cultural practices such as dance and theatre.

places.name: New Restaurant Ipoh Chicken Rice
places.text: Excellent chicken rice, tasty, affordable and in more comfortable atmosphere than Jalan Gasing outlets

places.name: Diving @ Aquaria KLCC
places.text: Take a plunge (literally) and explore Aquaria KLCC with the resident aquatic animals. The Cage Rage package takes you underwater in the safety of a cage. Be sure to say hello to the sharks when down there.
places.address: Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre Complex, Jl Pinang

places.name: Seri Negara
places.text: Seri Negara in Kuala Lumpur is a restored historic colonial mansion and cultural destination that opened to the public in December 2025 after years of closure and meticulous renovation, offering visitors a chance to explore its role in Malaysia’s journey to…

places.name: Bricks & Barrels
places.text: Large semi-opened air bar and restaurant with good happy hour promotions. Mix of local office workers along with expat who stay in the area. Be prepared to make reservations during large sporting events.

places.name: Little India
places.text: Beautifully restored street with all types of Indian shops and restaurants.

places.name: KLCC Park
places.text: A kid-friendly urban park surrounded by a concrete jungle. It boasts a children's pool and playground, walking/jogging tracks, a bird sanctuary, sculptures and 66 species of palm trees.
places.address: behind Petronas Towers (cross the Suria KLCC mall to get there)

places.name: Sri Maha Mariamman Temple
places.text: An elaborate Hindu temple known as the starting point of the yearly Thaipusam pilgrimage to the Batu Caves, where Hindu devotees haul portable altars pierced to their skin with 108 lances.

places.name: Bird Park
places.text: From beautiful peacocks to the alien-looking birds from all over the world, this 60-hectare bird park is home to 200 species.

places.name: Chan She Shu Yuen Temple
places.text: The clan house (kongsi) of the Chen (陳) family, this is the largest and oldest in KL, with the present version completed in 1906.

places.name: Restaurants along Jalan Radin Anum and Jalan Radin Bagus
places.text: A whole street's worth of eateries featuring cuisine from China, Taiwan and South Korea, too many to be listed in detail. As mentioned, this is the more happening part of Sri Petaling.
places.address: taxi or e-hailing from Bukit Jalil metro station is advisable

places.name: Souled Out
places.text: One of the original large restaurants/bars in Sri Hartamas. Always a good time here, drinks and food are of pretty high standards. Note that they do not serve pork here.

places.name: Nanyang Cafe
places.text: 2nd floor of Eko Cheras Mall. Check out their wanton mee, sandwiches and Yuenyeung (HK-styled coffee and milk tea mix).

places.name: Pavilion Kuala Lumpur
places.text: This luxury megamall is an anchor piece of the world-class urban development comprising two luxury residential towers, a corporate office.

places.name: Sri Kandaswamy Kovil
places.text: Opened in 1890 this Tamil temple is in at the eastern end of Jalan Scott. Photography and videography is no allowed within the temple.

places.name: Sin Sze Si Ya Temple
places.text: The oldest Chinese temple in Kuala Lumpur built in 1882. The temple is dedicated to Shen Kong, worshipped as the guardian deity for the local Chinese miners and houses several other deities, including the deified Yap Ah Loy, third Kapitan Cina of KL.

places.name: Butterfly Park
places.text: Walk-through tropical butterfly enclosure. Apparently the largest butterfly garden in the world spanning over 80,000 sq ft of landscaped garden with over 5,000 live butterflies, exotic plants, butterfly-host plants and ferns.

places.name: Istana Budaya
places.text: Istana Budaya (meaning Palace of Culture) is home to the National Theatre and is equipped with cutting edge stage, sound and lighting equipment on par with the top theatres around the world.

places.name: Uncle Don's
places.text: Western restaurant and bar, attached to the southern wing of Leisure Mall. Do check out their pizzas.

places.name: Muzium Diraja
places.text: The former palace of the electoral king of Malaysia, complete with all the royal splendor one might expect.

places.name: Guan Di Temple
places.text: Located across the road from the Sri Mahariamman Temple, this is one of two 19th-century Chinese temples in the district. Built in 1888, this temple is dedicated to the Han Dynasty/Three Kingdoms figure Guan Yu (aka Kwan Kung).

places.name: The Hornbill Restaurant & Cafe
places.text: Nice restaurant. The terrace of the restaurant faces the bird park. So even without paying the entrance fee to the bird park it is possible to observe some of the animals.

places.name: The Exchange TRX
places.text: Opened in 2023 it is considered the most popular mall in the city. It has a beautiful outdoor garden and the only Apple store in Malaysia on its rooftop.

places.name: Kwai Chai Hong
places.text: A back alley with beautiful murals depicting historic life in Chinatown. A few food and beverage outlets are located in the alley as well.

places.name: Rebung
places.text: Malay all-you-can-eat buffet. Four sessions per day: Breakfast, lunch, hi-tea, dinner. Very good online ratings.
places.address: On 5th floor of a multi-storey parking

places.name: Taman Dusun Bandar
places.text: An urban orchard park, near Muzium Diraja

places.name: LaLaport Bukit Bintang City Centre
places.text: Huge Japanese mall. Many lots still empty as of 2024 but the Gourmet Street - a pedestrian walkway with lost of restaurants - is worth a visit if you are nearby.

places.name: Thean Hou Temple
places.text: One of the largest and most ornate Chinese temples in the region. The six-tiered temple was built by the Hainanese community and is dedicated to Tian Hou, or the Heavenly Mother.

places.name: Laman Selera MADANI Tanglin
places.text: Food court with Malay cuisine like nasi lemak, and nasi campur.

places.name: Berjaya Times Square
places.text: It has 12 levels of retail with a total of 320,000 m² (3.5 million ft²). It is a middle-class shopping mall offering youth fashion targeted at the younger crowds.

places.name: Merdeka 118
places.text: A 118-storey skyscraper completed in 2023. At 680 m, it is the tallest building in Southeast Asia, and the second tallest building in the world, as of Feb 2024.

places.name: Titiwangsa Lake Gardens
places.text: Beautiful park with nice views to the city centre.

places.name: Fahrenheit 88
places.text: of lettable space spread over 5 levels of zoned shopping space. There are designated zones for Japanese and Korean fashion consisting of an entire floor each.

places.name: Stadium Merdeka
places.text: Tunku Abdul Rahman proclaimed the independence of the Federation of Malaya (Peninsular Malaysia) from British rule here on 31 August 1957. In fact, the stadium was purpose-built for that occasion.

places.name: Galeria Sri Perdana
places.text: The building, where this museum is housed, was the official residence of Tun Dr. Mahathir Mohamad, the fourth Prime Minister of Malaysia. Artefacts and personal collection of Dr.

places.name: Art Deco architecture
places.text: This stretch of Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman, starting from Sogo and Odeon Cinema in the north, and ending at Euro Moda in the south, contains a very large collection of Kuala Lumpur's art deco colonial buildings.

places.name: Cycle or hike on SWBC
places.text: If you need a break from the city hustle and bustle then try this: Walk or cycle on the Mid Valley-Dataran Merdeka Bike Lane, which was inaugurated in 2015.

places.name: Lot 10
places.text: When opened in 1991, it was considered the Harrods-equivalent of Malaysia housing designer outlets like Aigner and Versace. Time has however taken a toll on this mall which boasts a green facade.
places.address: Cnr Jl Bukit Bintang & Jl Sultan Ismail

places.name: Stadium Negara
places.text: Malaya's first sheltered stadium, it was built in the 1960s to somewhat complement the adjacent Merdeka Stadium.

places.name: Stroll around Kampung Baru
places.text: One of the most fascinating neighbourhoods of the whole city. The contrast between the charm of this unspoilt Malay quarter and the city skyscrapers only a stones throw away is what makes this place so special.
places.address: Take MRT Putrajaya to Raja Uda stop, LRT Kelana Jaya to Kampung Baru stop, or walk from KL

places.name: Plaza Low Yat
places.text: A good place for computer hardware, game consoles and handphones. A "must visit" for the tech inclined. All IT Hypermart (4th floor) is a good one-stop shop, but there are dozens of specialist computing boutiques for the enthusiast.

places.name: Victoria Institution
places.text: Though not exactly a tourist spot, this school, easily recognisable by its clock tower on its main block, is the oldest existing operational public school in Kuala Lumpur, having been founded in 1893 and relocated to its present site in 1929.

places.name: Bazaar Baru Chow Kit
places.text: Boasting the title as the largest wet market in Kuala Lumpur this market gives a glimpse of how ordinary Malaysians do their daily shopping.

places.name: Al-Bukhari Foundation Mosque
places.text: Beautiful mosque well worth a visit. Located next to the Victoria Institution.

places.name: Starhill Gallery
places.text: Adjoining the JW Marriott Hotel. The nearest station to this mall is Monorail Bukit Bintang. Starhill is a literally an English translation of “Bukit Bintang”.

places.name: Masjid India Bazaar
places.text: A covered bazaar stretching out from LRT Masjid Jamek, along Jalan Melayu towards Masjid India, quite similar in feel to the more famous Jalan Petaling (with a similar plastic overhang) but not as large or crowded -- not necessarily a bad thing.

places.name: Megamall & The Gardens
places.text: This really is "mega" with over 430 shops crammed into what claims to be one of South-East Asia's largest shopping malls. Anchor tenants include hypermarket AEON Big (Malaysian branch of AEON Japan), local store Metrojaya.

places.name: Chin Woo Stadium
places.text: Not quite a stadium, but more of a sports hall/badminton court and community centre for the local Chinese community. Do check out its public pool.

places.name: Sungei Wang Plaza
places.text: A popular place among local teenagers where fashion clothes, shoes, accessories and other trinkets and local designer clothes can be found with affordable price.

places.name: Suria KLCC
places.text: Suria KLCC is one of Malaysia's premier shopping destinations due to its location beneath the Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur City Centre.
places.address: Cnr Jl P Ramlee & Jl Ampang

places.name: Pasar Malam
places.text: A long night market spanning the entire length of the 'lorong'. This weekly night market is an experience whether you are looking for a bargain, local products, or just an authentic Malaysian market experience.

places.name: Bangsar Village II
places.text: This is another favourite with those staying around Bangsar & Damansara Heights neighbourhood. Bangsar Village 2 is linked to the original Bangsar Village by a covered pedestrian bridge.

places.name: Royal Selangor Club
places.text: Founded by the British in 1884.

places.name: Campbell Complex
places.text: Great shopping centre to buy textiles. Site of the infamous Campbell Complex fire in 1976, regarded as Malaysia's own "Towering Inferno".

places.name: Bangsar Shopping Centre
places.text: Better known as BSC, this mini shopping centre is a favourite among expats and the locals staying around the Bangsar & Damansara Heights neighbourhood. Plenty of cafes & restaurants - a good spot to meet up with friends.

places.name: Petaling Street
places.text: The bustling centre of this district. Chinese-styled arches mark the entrances of this street. A relatively tame area during the day that comes alive in the evenings with stalls selling fake handbags, shoes, watches, sunglasses, DVDs and other various items.

places.name: Avenue K
places.text: Opposite Kuala Lumpur City Centre. With its bold tagline, "style has a new address", the complex is a hip shopping haven complimented by a classy, city-living address, "K Residence".

places.name: Lot 10 Hutong
places.text: This shopping mall in the Golden Triangle has a collection of 20 street vendors who were invited to relocate in the food court.
places.address: Cnr Jl Bukit Bintang & Jl Sultan Ismail

places.name: Second-hand/out-of-season cloths
places.text: Near this GPS marker you will find two Muslim-run cloths shops which sell dirt-cheap second-hand and out-of-season cloths, both to the west and east inside the buildings on the ground floor.

places.name: Jaya Restoran
places.text: Great selection of Indian dishes. Very fresh ingredients. Especially the lunch buffet is highly recommended.

places.name: Plaza City One
places.text: Textile and fashion stores congregate here. At the second floor above ground level there is a food court (see 'Eat' section below).

places.name: Central Market
places.text: Kuala Lumpur's grand old market was opened in 1888 as a normal wet market, but the current building was actually built in 1937. Slated for demolition in the 1980s, it was luckily preserved after public outcry, and refurbished as a cultural market.
places.address: Cnr Jl Hang Kasturi & Jl Tun Tan Cheng Lock

places.name: Peter's Pork Noodle
places.text: This food stall in the well hidden Money's corner food court is considered one of the best pork noodle places in whole Kuala Lumpur. Try to avoid the peak hours (weekdays from 11:30 to 13:30).

places.name: Semua House
places.text: Fashion, cosmetics, perfume, and jewellery. There is a Burger King store at the ground-level entrance. Food court located one floor below ground.

places.name: Nasi Kandar Pelita
places.text: A huge outlet of Malaysia's largest nasi kandar chain, with long queues snaking out at lunchtime.

places.name: Bijan
places.text: 3 Jln Ceylon - Modern-styled décor in a home-like setting with outdoor verandah-garden compliments the well prepared (though perhaps slightly overpriced) Malaysian food.

places.name: Mydin Wholesale Emporium
places.text: Has a supermarket on the 3rd floor. It is also a bus hub.
places.address: Bangunan Sinar Kota Jalan Tun Perak

places.name: GS Gills
places.text: The top sporting goods distributes in Mayalsia, carrying all sorts of sporting equipment and attire.
places.address: 9th Floor, Wisma Harwant, 106 Jalan Tuanku Adbul Rahman

places.name: Annalakshmi Vegetarian Restaurant
places.text: Famous vegetarian restaurant at the Temple of Fine Arts, with occasional cultural shows. Food is no longer priced based on a pay-as-you-wish model; the restaurant charges set prices for food.

places.name: Chat Masala
places.text: This vegetarian restaurant serves mock meat. Go for the "mutton" or "chicken" briyani, tea-time specials like pani puri or bhel puri, then wash it down with filter coffee.

places.name: Pertama Complex
places.text: Opened in 1976 as Kuala Lumpur's third shopping mall, and still good for cheap shoes, leather ware and other knick-knacks.

places.name: Jalan Alor Food Stalls
places.text: In the heart of KL and within walking distance from the shopping district of Bukit Bintang, Jalan Alor has become one of the most popular food streets in KL.

places.name: 99 Speed Mart no. 1292
places.text: Mini market chain. There are many 99 Speed Marts around KL.
places.address: 34 G Jalan Hang Kasturi City Center

places.name: Sogo Shopping Complex
places.text: Probably the biggest department store you will ever see, with 10 floors of shopping, dining and entertainment. If you budget permits, you can shop here for everything from clothing to high-tech toys.

places.name: Glutton Street Market
places.text: Another street full of food stalls similar to Jalan Alor, but a lot less touristy and more authentic.

places.name: KK Super Mart
places.text: 24 hour convenience store. There is another store at Jalan Sultan.

places.name: Sunway Putra Mall
places.text: Opened in 1987 and reopened in 2015 after a two-year refurbishment project, this mall is connected to the PWTC metro station and Putra Komuter station by a linkbridge, as well as the Putra World Trade Centre, featuring a convention centre and home to…

places.name: Dharma Realm Monastery Canteen
places.text: Great vegetarian food prepared by volunteers. Earnings are used to maintain the temple. A favourite among local office workers. The food is free of charge on Fridays and Sundays.
places.address: Behind Kun Yam Thong Temple, just a stone's throw away from KLCC along Jalan Ampang

places.name: Saravanaa Bhavan
places.text: Clean restaurant serving authentic South Indian cuisine. All food is vegetarian.

places.name: Bunn Choon Restaurant
places.text: Old-time Chinese kopitiam, operating since the 19th century, serving noodles, dim sum, as well as pastries.
places.hours: Daily 7:30AM to about 4PM, depending on stocks

places.name: Super Noodle House
places.text: One of the best Hong Kong-style restaurants in KL. Menu includes porridge, wantan mee or chicken rice. Good food with reasonable pricing.
places.address: LG-001, Lower Ground, Sungai Wang Shopping Centre, Jalan Sultan Ismail

places.name: Wisma Shen (Haniffa Department Store)
places.text: StarPoints Hotel occupies the upper floors of the building. On the ground level there is a Haniffa Department Store. Do check out Haniffa for its large collection of chocolates.

places.name: Quill City Mall
places.text: A shopping mall in downtown KL, it is about 3 to 5 minutes' walk from Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman itself. Features seven retail levels, eateries, a cinema and a NSK supermarket.

places.name: Kim Lian Kee
places.text: Right in the middle of Petaling Street, at the crossroads with Jalan Hang Lekir. In business since the 1920s, this stall was regarded as the inventor of KL-styled hokkien fried mee.

places.name: Lulu Hypermarket
places.text: Arab-owned LuLu Hypermarket opened its first store in Malaysia here. Hypermarket and fresh produce on the ground level. Ethnic fashion and pharmacy on the first floor, electronics, stationery, furnishing and sporting goods on the second floor.
places.address: Lot 159 Persiaran CapSquare Off Jalan Munshi Abdullah

places.name: Passage Thru' India
places.text: An excellent Indian restaurant that offers both northern and southern Indian cuisine. Favorites here include the Chicken Beriyani, Chicken Tandoori, Chukka Mutton, Fried Fish, Malabar Avial and the slightly expensive but very tasty PTI Prawn masala.
places.address: 4 Jl Delima (several other locations through Malaysia)

places.name: Soong Kee Beef Noodles
places.text: This is a well-known KL beef noodle shop, it is said to have started operating since 1945. It serves the noodles "dry" with beef mince while the beef balls are given separately in a bowl of soup.

places.name: Devi's Corner
places.text: Great banana leaf restaurant. It is not as famous as the nearby Nirwana banana leaf restaurant, but cheaper and - according to many locals - has better tasting food.

places.name: Busana Menara Mara
places.text: State-owned commercial centre featuring Malay textile, fashion, arts and crafts stores. Level 3 is home to MARA Digital, dedicated to computers and IT equipment.
places.address: Menara MARA, Lot C, 232, Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman

places.name: Sin Kiew Yee Shin Kee Beef Noodles
places.text: Also very traditional beef noodles like before, but more choices and also very popular with locals and tourists. 3 different noodles, 3 different ways of beef, dry or wet.
places.address: right outside west the northern exit of Petaling Street

places.name: Restoran Ganesh
places.text: A fantastic place, Indian food that you don't get at most places, served on banana leaves.
places.address: next to the Court Hill Ganesh temple

places.name: Maju Junction
places.text: This vacant shopping mall is a pit stop for pedestrians walking from Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman to Quill City Mall and the Sultan Ismail metro station.

places.name: Lebuh Ampang banana leaf restaurants
places.text: Located adjacent to Masjid Jamek station, the street is lined with Indian banana leaf rice shops, just make your pick. One of them is Lakshmi Villas. For purely vegetarian food, you can try Saravanaa Bhavan or Bakti Woodlands.
places.address: Gate B of Masjid Jamek metro station, then walk along Jalan Tun Perak (Mountbatten Road)

places.name: The Social
places.text: Popular bar and restaurant.Can get quite noisy due to the large crowd.

places.name: Central Market Food Court
places.text: Food court on Central Market's mezzanine floor, one of the few air-conditioned eating places in the area.

places.name: Sahara Tent
places.text: Large, authentic and popular Middle Eastern eatery in Ain Arabia, KL's Little Arabia.
places.address: 87 Jalan Berangan, off Jalan Bukit Bintang

places.name: Kedai Makanan Daun Pisang Vinny Jeyaa
places.text: typical Indian restaurant (as for Malaysia) but with exceptionally wide choice of Indian delicacies (both veg and non-veg).

places.name: Capital Cafe
places.text: Opposite Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman from the Sogo mall. Known to be one of the oldest cafes along Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman. Founded in the 1940s, popular until now.
places.address: 213, Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman, City Centre

places.name: EEST @ The Westin Kuala Lumpur
places.text: EEST is a prominent Asian restaurant in Kuala Lumpur. Savour the blend of authentic flavours specially selected from Asian cultures right here in Kuala Lumpur.

places.name: RA Nasi Lemak
places.text: Serving up the Malaysian breakfast favourite, Nasi Lemak, and a range of drinks including Teh Tarik. A plate of rice is given to you then you add whatever you like on a self-serve basis.

places.name: Zhing Kong Restaurant
places.text: Chinese kopitiam, at the ground floor of Starlight Hotel.

places.name: Bistro de Paris
places.text: The French dining experience from aperitif to digestif, ranging from steak frites to crême brulée. Open daily from 11AM until late.

places.name: Ho Kow Hainam Kopitiam
places.text: Hainanese kopitiam in business since 1956 serving typical koptiam fare (nasi lemak, chicken hor fun, kaya toast etc). Watch out for the long queues; advisable to come early.
places.hours: Daily 7:30AM-3PM, though stocks may run out early

places.name: Yut Kee Restaurant
places.text: A true KL establishment, this Chinese coffeeshop is famous for its Hainanese-style chicken chop and roti babi, pork sandwich. It has relocated to a larger building behind its former site.

places.name: Texas Chicken
places.text: One of only 2 remaining Western fast-food joints in this area (and the only one to operate 24/7), after a McDonald's at the entrance of Petaling Street ceased operations a few years ago, followed by a former Subway opposite Kotaraya complex.
places.address: Lot G.02, Ground Floor, Wisma Fui Chiu, No. 32, Jalan Tun Tan Cheng Lock

places.name: Plaza City One Food Court
places.text: Check out the food court on Level 2 of Plaza City One for its Indian, Pakistani and Bangladeshi cuisine. Recommended: Hanif Mughal Food (stall 5), Nasi Arab (stall 3) and Punjabi Vegetarian Food (stall 8).

places.name: El Cerdo
places.text: German-run eatery with kitschy pig-themed decor specializing in all things pork, particularly Spanish treats like jamón serrano and whole suckling pig, complete with ceremonial plate-breaking.

places.name: KFC
places.text: The other Western fast-food joint in this area (coincidentally, fried chicken as well).

places.name: Neroteca
places.text: Italian restaurant and deli, specialized in pork meat. They serve great Italian hearty food with one of a great selection of Italian cured meats and cheeses, also for take away.

places.name: Kudu bin Abdul Nasi Kandar
places.text: Famous Nasi Kandar restaurant near the junction with Jalan Sultan Ismail. The late Malaysian artist P. Ramlee was reportedly a fan - his former film studio was located across the street.
places.address: 335, Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman, Medan Tuanku

places.name: Coliseum Cafe and Bar
places.text: A KL legend, this colonial-style hangout hasn't changed its appearance or staff in over 90 years. In the late 2010s, this restaurant has expanded to Mid Valley, Petaling Jaya and Subang Jaya.

places.name: Horizon Grill
places.text: Great fusion food with stunning views towards the Petronas Towers.

places.name: Luna Bar
places.text: Menara PanGlobal 34F, Jalan Punchak (off Jl P. Ramlee). - Super-chic breezy rooftop bar with a pool in the middle and the best night views in town. Show up early to grab a romantic windowside niche.

places.name: Reggae Bar
places.text: It is a hostel bar so it is popular with backpackers. They also serve Asian and Western food. Also a hostel!

places.name: Sky Bar
places.text: Incredible bar with great views over the city and the Twin Towers.Located on the top floor of the Traders Hotel, it is built around the Hotel swimming pool.

places.name: Heli Lounge
places.text: Amazing location on a helipad high above the city with amazing views.

stays.name: Somerset Kuala Lumpur
stays.text: Offers 207 apartments that range from the studio to three-bedroom layouts with modern kitchen, Wi-Fi.

stays.name: Villa Samadhi Kuala Lumpur
stays.text: 10 minutes drive from town, housing 21 contemporary Asian-inspired rooms, with each spanning 600-2000 square feet.

stays.name: Midtown Villa
stays.text: A conveniently located and quiet hotel. Standard rooms. Helpful and friendly staff. Unreliable internet connections.

stays.name: Hotel Caliber
stays.text: 45-46, Jalan 5/101C, Off Jalan Kaskas, Cheras Commercial Centre, Taman Cheras. The hotel offers 132 tastefully furnished rooms at reasonable rates.

stays.name: Hotel Sri Petaling
stays.text: Some of its amenities are tour and travel information desk, dry cleaning/laundry, and business center with comprehensive service.

stays.name: The Majestic Hotel
stays.text: Considered one of the best hotels in the city.

stays.name: Joy Inn
stays.text: Hotel built on top of grocery store. The rooms are small but comparable to other hotels in the area.

stays.name: PODs The Backpackers Home
stays.text: Comfortable and clean. Free wheelie tours offered weekly and a very interesting open stage event every first Friday of the month.

stays.name: YMCA Hostel
stays.text: Like most YMCA Hostels this one feels sterile, It is clean and safe. Make sure to check their website for guest restrictions.

stays.name: Hotel Sentral
stays.text: Nice and clean hotel with good online ratings.

stays.name: Hilton
stays.text: This hotel which opened around 2005, is adjacent to the KL Sentral train station and the Le Meridien. The Hilton has rooms with open bathrooms and plasma TVs.

stays.name: Le Meridien
stays.text: Adjacent to the KL Sentral train station. Opened in 2004, has a splendid lobby and modern rooms with views of the nearby gardens (or the roof of KL Sentral if you pick the wrong side).

stays.name: Lotus Hotel
stays.text: Budget hotel just behind the Masjid Jamek metro station, at the entrance of the Masjid India bazaar.

stays.name: Aloft Kuala Lumpur Sentral
stays.text: Consists of 482 rooms & suites, multiple meeting rooms, ballrooms, restaurants. It is a modern property 950 metres away from the Nu Sentral Mall.

stays.name: The St. Regis
stays.text: Opened in 2017; five-star hotel. Many rooms have a beautiful view to the Botanical Garden. The hotel has consistently high online ratings.

stays.name: Swiss Hotel
stays.text: Not affiliated with Swissôtel, so do not expect the same level of service. Just across the LRT tracks from Dataran Merdeka.

stays.name: Hostel Travel Hub
stays.text: Run by a friendly Sri Lankan family. Full A/C and breakfast included with free Wi-Fi and no curfews. Clean, very safe and basic.

stays.name: Ascott Sentral Kuala Lumpur
stays.text: The property features 157 fully furnished serviced apartments with easy access to KL Sentral railway station and Kuala Lumpur International Airport.

stays.name: Hotel Petaling
stays.text: Clean and cheap hostel along Petaling Street run by Malaysian-Chinese owners. Good online ratings.

stays.name: Rainforest Bed & Breakfast
stays.text: Boutique budget hotel with dorm bed and private rooms. Beautiful building with tasteful, rainforest-themed decorations.

stays.name: Citin Hotel Masjid Jamek
stays.text: Opened 2009 smack dab in the middle of the Masjid India bazaar, offers small but surprisingly slick, quiet and sparkling clean rooms.

stays.name: The Original Backpacker's Travellers Inn
stays.text: No-frills, budget accommodation close to Bukit Bintang and Chinatown. 5 min walk from the Pasar Seni train station. 8 bed Dorms.

stays.name: Etika Inn
stays.text: Unassuming with its small, easy-to-miss entrance. Large rooms, attached bathrooms with hot water shower, clean. Wifi is available in all the rooms.

stays.name: Kuala Lumpur International Hotel
stays.text: Spacious accommodation, all equipped with air condition, cable television, phone with voicemail system. Facilities and services are function rooms, business centre and Wi-Fi Internet access.

stays.name: Sunshine Bedz
stays.text: A small and friendly family run hostel with modern but basic facilities. Breakfast is included in the price and free Wi-Fi/computers also available.

stays.name: Ancasa Express @ Pudu
stays.text: All rooms equipped with air-conditioning, telephone, private toilet and bath. Some of its facilities and services are cafe, transit lounge, wake-up call, parking, airport and city transfers.

stays.name: Leo Palace Hotel
stays.text: Slightly above average budget hotel, 5 min walk to Titiwangsa metro/monorail. Rooftop pool.

stays.name: Heritage Hotel
stays.text: This place might have shut down! Please check and update. Housed in KL's beautiful old railway station, one stop from KL Sentral.

stays.name: Chinatown Boutique Hotel
stays.text: Some rooms are smaller than others and some have bigger windows, so you may want to check first. Windows are all quite thick and sound proof so noise from Jalan Sultan is not a problem.

stays.name: Paper Plane Hostel
stays.text: A clean hostel with plenty of shower stalls, laundry service, and friendly workers at the front desk available 24/7.

stays.name: Le Village
stays.text: Hostel in the middle of Petaling Street street market. Good online ratings.

stays.name: Ormond The Chow Kit
stays.text: Previously the Tune Hotel, until it was refurbished as the Ormond Chow Kit.

stays.name: Matahari Lodge
stays.text: Clean hostel/guesthouse, with private A/C single, double rooms and mixed dormitory with shared showers. 24/7 reception with security system.

stays.name: Bintang Garden Hotel
stays.text: 51 air-con small rooms with free Wi-Fi Internet, hot water, cable TV (very bad signal--don't even bother taking the remote from the lobby).

stays.name: Bintang Warisan Hotel
stays.text: 68 Jl Bukit Bintang. Hotel that offers traditional look, feel and service.

stays.name: Sheraton Imperial
stays.text: Opposite the Quill City Mall. Rooms have plasma TV, butler service, walk in closet.

stays.name: The 5 Elements Hotel
stays.text: Boutique hotel inspired by traditional Wu Xing (五行) philosophy. Here, water, wood, fire, earth and metal set the theme.

stays.name: Silka Maytower
stays.text: Consists of hotel suites and serviced apartments. Facilities provided: gym, pool, car park. La Maison restaurant located at the lobby.

stays.name: Concorde
stays.text: A decent mid-range hotel that is fairly good value with all the typical amenities you would expect, including a pool.

stays.name: Twin Tower View
stays.text: 2-bedroom apartment in a condominium opposite PWTC train station. View across KL city centre. A/C, ceiling fans, Wi-Fi, swimming pool.

stays.name: Hotel Chinatown 2
stays.text: Popular with foreigners. At night it may be noisy like all hotels on this street (centre of the Chinatown night market).

stays.name: Stripes Hotel
stays.text: Near Quill City Mall and Medan Tuanku Monorail station.

stays.name: Swiss Garden Residences
stays.text: Embracing 478 serviced apartments and offering a variety of one bedroom, two bedroom apartment suites and four bedroom penthouse suites.

stays.name: Travelodge City Centre
stays.text: Decent hotel adjacent to Pasar Seni metro station and near Central Market.

stays.name: Lavana Hotel
stays.text: Occupying the top floors of Bangunan Mariamman (next to Vinny Jeyaa restaurant).

stays.name: Ascott Kuala Lumpur
stays.text: 221 apartments that come fully-furnished with a home entertainment system, kitchen and broadband Internet access.

stays.name: Olympic Sports Hotel
stays.text: Hotel with two conference halls, attached to the offices of Malaysia's Olympic Committee.

stays.name: Regal Park Hotel
stays.text: 3-star hotel with average online ratings. 10-min walk to China Town.

stays.name: Berjaya Times Square Hotel
stays.text: In the mammoth Berjaya Times Square shopping mall complex. Has a large conference centre.

stays.name: Dorsett Regency Hotel Kuala Lumpur
stays.text: Fully A/C rooms with 32" LCD TV, satellite channels, in-house movies, free internet connection, and mini-bar. Spa, lounge by the pool.

stays.name: Four Points by Sheraton
stays.text: The newest and largest hotel in the area, having been completed in 2019. 4-star, with outdoor pool and gym.

stays.name: Pacific Express Hotel Central Market
stays.text: Hotel with rooftop pool and gym. This building was a bank in the 1960s. MyNews convenience store at ground floor.

stays.name: Hotel Maya
stays.text: All rooms have satellite TV, wifi.

stays.name: Parkroyal Kuala Lumpur
stays.text: Offers daily scheduled shuttle service to Kuala Lumpur City Centre (KLCC) and Aquaria KLCC.

stays.name: Grand Millennium Kuala Lumpur
stays.text: 468 guestrooms including 30 suites, all with floor-to-ceiling windows that provide sweeping views of the city skyline.

stays.name: JW Marriott
stays.text: Marriott's flagship hotel in Kuala Lumpur, decorated in a Malaysian style and conveniently located on Jalan Bukit Bintang near the shopping district.

stays.name: Westin
stays.text: Extremely modern and well-equipped but quite lacking in identity, with nothing but the view to remind you that you're in Malaysia.

stays.name: Shangri-La
stays.text: Started in the early 1980s, it has been kept up to date with the owners continually reinvesting in the property. Internet is free in the room and the hotel.

stays.name: Ritz Carlton
stays.text: This hotel and residence is connected to Starhill Gallery and hosts the Spa Village, one of the best in Malaysia.

stays.name: Mandarin Oriental

destinations.name: Labuan
destinations.intro: Labuan is a federal territory of Malaysia. It comprises one large and six smaller islands in off the coast of Sabah in Malaysia.
destinations.eat_notes: All food, especially fresh seafood, is extremely well priced. But if you get the locals as a guide, they can show you some cheaper alternatives instead. The most famous local dessert is "Coconut Pudding", which you wouldn't be able to find in anywhere else.

places.name: The Chimney
places.text: The Chimney is just a short drive from the town just like any other destination due to the island size. This 106 feet (30 m) high red brick stack, also known by the local as Punil, is an artifact from Labuan's coal mining era (1847–1912).

places.name: Bird Park

destinations.name: Melaka
destinations.intro: Malacca City (Malay: Bandaraya Melaka, and officially Melaka City) is a city and the capital of the state of Malacca, Malaysia. Malacca is a vibrant old city with a unique historical and cultural background. The city centre is listed as a , along with George Town, Penang.
destinations.eat_notes: Besides the usual Malaysian fare, you'll be able to sample some rather peculiar Malaccan food. On top of the list is of course Peranakan or Baba-Nyonya food, which used to be totally uncommercialised and confined to the kitchens of old grandmothers.

notes.title: School holidays
notes.text: Late May to June and most of December are school holidays: book early, and expect traffic and queues at anything family-friendly.

notes.title: Hari Raya Aidilfitri
notes.text: The biggest holiday of the year. Cities empty out, highways jam with people heading home, and many eateries close for the first few days. The date moves about 11 days earlier every year.

notes.title: Chinese New Year
notes.text: Lanterns, lion dances and open houses. Many Chinese-run shops and eateries close for the first two or three days, so plan your meals.

places.name: Cheng Hoon Teng Temple
places.text: Oldest Chinese temple in Malaysia and has an inscription dating 1685 commemorating the deeds of by Kapitan China Li Wei King.

places.name: Christ Church
places.text: his church was built between 1741 and 1753. It replaced a Portuguese church, which was shattered. Bricks were shipped from Zeeland in the Netherlands. On the floor of the church you will find Dutch tombstones.

places.name: Dutch Square
places.text: Beautiful square around Christ Church and the Stadhuys. On this square you will find the Tang Beng Swee Clock Tower, it looks Dutch, but it is not. It was built in 1886.

places.name: Jonker, Heeren and adjacent streets
places.text: This is the residential heart of Old Malacca just west of the Malacca River, with its narrow winding streets, beautifully decorated houses, tiny shops, temples and mosques.

places.name: Masjid Kampung Hulu
places.text: Built in 1728, it's one of the oldest functioning mosques in Melaka together with Masjid Kampung Kling and Masjid Tengkera (Tranquerah), Jln Tengkera see the mixed architecture of Chinese, Javanese and Arab on the minarets and the roofs.

places.name: Porta de Santiago
places.text: The remains of the old Portuguese fort A Famosa, what you can see now is a mostly Dutch reconstruction, bearing the VOC coat of arms.

places.name: Saint Paul's Church
places.text: It was built in 1521, by the Portuguese. It became a fortress in 1567, until 1596. After the Dutch siege it became St Paul's, before it was known as Nossa Senhora da Annunciada (Our Lady of Annunciation).

places.name: Baba Nyonya Heritage Museum
places.text: Step back in time with a visit to this museum which is an actual historic Peranakan townhouse complete with the original antique furniture, and a great way to have a glimpse into the life of a wealthy Peranakan family during the colonial era.

places.name: Malay and Islamic World Museum
places.text: The ground floor hosts temporary exhibits, the first floor showcases Malay history (particularly before the sultanate), the second floor has exhibits on Indonesia.

places.name: Maritime Museum
places.text: The main historical exhibits are hosted inside a replica of the Flor de la Mar, a 16th-century Portuguese ship. A building includes additional exhibits on modern maritime activity and sea life.

places.name: Melaka Islamic Museum
places.text: A general introduction to Islam and the Islamic world, with a section on Islam in Malaysia and local scholars.

places.name: Melaka Sultanate Palace Museum
places.text: Below the hill you will find this museum (Melaka Cultural Museum). It is a reconstruction of the istana of the sultan Mansur Shah. It was built in 1985.
places.hours: Sat- Mon Wed Thu 09:00-18:00, Tue Fri 12:15–14:45

places.name: Stadthuys
places.text: Completed in 1660. It is a reproduction of the former Stadhuis (town hall) of the Frisian town of Hoorn in the Netherlands which existed from 1420 until 1796.

places.name: Melaka UMNO Museum
places.text: Museum about the United Malays National Organisation, the dominant political party of Malaysia for most of its history.

places.name: Youth Museum/Melaka Art Gallery
places.text: The Youth Museum is on the ground floor, the Art Gallery on the second level. You can have a bird's eye view of Dutch Square from a window on the second level.

places.name: Bukit China
places.text: Bukit China is one of the largest Chinese cemeteries outside mainland China. Graves can be found here that go back to the late Ming dynasty (mid-17th century).

places.name: Melaka Straits Mosque
places.text: A mosque built on the man-made island, Pulau Melaka, just off the coast the city. Spectacular at evening and night.

places.name: Poh San Teng Temple
places.text: This temple is at the foot of Bukit China and next to the King's Well, was founded in 1795 by Kapitan China Chua Su Cheong as a graveyard temple. The main deity is Fu-te Zhen Shen.

places.name: Portuguese Settlement
places.text: Here is where the descendants of the Portuguese who conquered Malacca in 1511 live today.
places.address: Take bus 17 (destination "Ujong Pasir and Bandar Hilir") from Melaka Sentral

places.name: St John's Hill and Fort
places.text: Malacca's other fortress is on top of St John's Hill in Bandar Hilir, south of the city. Pretty views of the surroundings from the top. Malacca Town Bus (green) No.

places.name: Morten Village
places.text: A village of traditional houses, it is on the west bank of the Melaka River.

places.name: The Shore Oceanarium
places.text: Not a very big aquarium with a quiz program for kids.

places.name: Macau Gallery
places.text: Gallery about Macau housed in a historical 2-story British bungalow.

places.name: Sea-Turtle Sanctuary
places.text: Information center is at the Padang Kemunting beach (28 km away from Melaka Sentral), where they have a few information boards and dozen of the hawksbill turtles living in an aquarium.
places.hours: Information center works 10:00-16:00, closed on Mon and public holidays

places.name: Geok Hu Keng Temple
places.text: This temple has a history of 130 years. Managed by local communities, the temple was incorporated under the management of Cheng Hoon Teng in 2000.

places.name: Pulau Besar
places.text: Big Island off the coast of Malacca, about 13 km from the mainland. It has a few resorts, the Tomb of Syarifah Rodziah and the Pulau Besar Museum.
places.address: drive to Anjung Batu and then take a 20-minutes ferry ride

places.name: Tanjung Keling
places.text: The nearest beach from Malacca just 10 km away. Tanjong Keling Mosque and the grave of Hang Tuah, the legendary Malay warrior, are close to the beach. Getting there: take a bus from Jalan Tun Ali bus terminal in Malacca.

places.name: Pantai Kundur
places.text: A small fishing village with a nice beach 2 km away from Tanjung Keling.

places.name: Tanjung Bidara
places.text: One of the Malacca’s most popular white sandy beaches. It has facilities for canoeing, water-skiing and jet-skiing.

places.name: Malacca Duck Tour
places.text: This is an old military amphibious vehicle that has been adapted for amphibious tourist trips around Melaka city and moving towards the sea and come back up.

places.name: Taming Sari Tower
places.text: The 110 m-tower seats 66 people at a time, taking them on a 7-min ride for a view of Melaka City. The ascent takes 1 min, you have 5 min on the top and 1 min for the descent.
places.hours: every 30 min on the hour and half-hour, 10:00-23:00 daily.

places.name: Beyond Treasures
places.text: Woodcrafts, including Asian masks, antiques and souvenirs.

places.name: The Orangutan House
places.text: Has cool T-shirts, and paintings for sale.

places.name: Jonker Gallery
places.text: A lovely art gallery of contemporary art work by Titi Kwok, the work is beautiful and the prices even better.

places.name: J. Manik Sdn. Bhd
places.text: A shop where they sell authentic Nyonya kebaya and kasut manik-manik (beaded shoes for the ladies). Nyonya kebaya and kasut manik-manik are the tradisional attires of the Baba Nyonya and the Peranakan Heritage.

places.name: The Eight Immortals House
places.text: Famous local tea shop selling a range of tea from China and Taiwan as well as offering tea ceremony classes.

places.name: Red Handicrafts
places.text: Local artist Ray Tan creates and sells traditional handmade souvenirs with a Chinese-Malaysian flair. Highlights include chuāng huā (窗花) or red paper cuttings, silk-screen T-shirts and wall hangings, embroidery and old Chinese finger puppets.

places.name: Jonkers Walk
places.text: A night market held every weekend evening to late night from 18:00-00:00.

places.name: Mahkota Parade
places.text: Over 200 shops. Anchor tenants are Parkson Grand Departmental Store and Giant Supermarket.
places.address: located in Bandar Hilir opposite Padang Pahlawan

places.name: Bee Bee (Lian Choo) Homemade Pineapple Tarts
places.text: When they say 'homemade' here, they really mean it literally. There's no other homemade delicacy in Malacca that can beat this place as both its production and location are authentically traditional.

places.name: Baba Charlie Nyonya Cake
places.text: Another hidden gem where you can buy all kinds of authentic Nyonya kuihs you can ever imagined under one roof. Too many to choose from, you wish you could camp there and try it all.

places.name: Jalan Kee Ann
places.text: Open-air eating stalls for locals and visitors. It is a good place to eat and see the world go by while eating in the open air. Local cuisines include won ton mee, popiah, yew keow, sugar cane water, sup kambing, MN and satay.

places.name: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
places.text: Decent purveyor taste-wise of Hainanese chicken rice balls and other treats.

places.name: My Chicken Rice
places.text: Another possible chicken rice ball option.

places.name: Hing Loong Taiwanese Noodle
places.text: Located out of the town center but have been discovered by many non-Malaccans. Tasty beef, fried pork chop or pig trotter noodles in soup or in sauce.

places.name: Tengkera Mee Soup
places.text: Many varieties of noodles are served Chinese style by a Malay/Muslim vendor and are Halal.
places.hours: Open from mid-afternoon until when the noodles are sold out.

places.name: Pak Putra Tandoori
places.text: Very popular (touristy) North Indian restaurant. Food tastes very good. Famous for their naan and tandoori.

places.name: Restoran Selvam
places.text: Popular for their vegetable banana leaf rice. Extra vegetable sauces and papadum are free. Service can be almost rude sometimes but the food tastes great.

places.name: The Seafarer Restaurant
places.text: Enjoy a variety of Peranakan, Chinese, Western and seafood cuisines encompanied by gentle sea breeze ambience. Opens daily with nightly live music. Dance floor,big screen projector & bar with virtual golf simulation are available.

places.name: Portuguese Settlement
places.text: Popular for its fried squid, Portuguese baked fish. Local favorite stalls are numbered 1 and 7.

places.name: Limau Limau Cafe
places.text: Wide selections of fresh juices, milkshakes and lassi, with no water or sugar added. They sell Lavazza coffee.

places.name: Exodus Lounge (Formerly Known As Krabau Rock Cafe)
places.text: Exodus Lounge, formerly known as Krabau Cafe is now one of the latest best chill out place at Jonker Walk, Melaka. Malaysia.

places.text: A great crowd fusion of westerners and locals, a best chill out place with some cold beer on a warm night with live music and a small open dance floor. Great place to mingle away.

places.name: Calanthe Art Cafe
places.text: Adorable art cafe decorated with old Malaccan trinkets, best known for their excellent laksa and wide assortment of coffee (coffea liberica) from all 13 Malaysian states.

destinations.name: Port Dickson
destinations.intro: Port Dickson is a popular beach destination in the state of Negeri Sembilan, Peninsular Malaysia. About 60 km from Kuala Lumpur, Port Dickson, or PD to locals, is about an hour's drive from Kuala Lumpur along the North-South Highway and about 32 km from Seremban.
destinations.eat_notes: For those who are into gastronomic activities, one can get a taste of the hot and spicy local cuisine. There’s fish cooked in thick gravy of coconut milk and the killer cili padi which is guaranteed to make your mouth and eyes smart.

places.name: Tanjung Tuan
places.text: The Portuguese built the Cape Rachardo lighthouse in the 16th century. The lighthouse guided ships to the Port of Malacca. It is still operational today.

places.name: Army Museum Port Dickson
places.text: This museum is the latest attraction in Port Dickson. Some vehicles and aircraft used by the Royal Malaysian Army is displayed here. There also a Communist tunnel.
places.address: Next to a Malaysian Army camp

places.name: Lukut Museum and Fort
places.text: About 7 km from Port Dickson. Raja Jumaat was a 19th-century Bugis warrior. The fort was built in 1847 to control the lucrative tin trade in the area.

places.name: Fort Kempas
places.text: About 23 km from the lighthouse, there is a small village called Keramat Ujung Pasir. Here you will find a 15th-century tomb of a leading historical personality, Ulama Sheikh Ahmad Makhtum, with its famous carved megalith.

places.name: Blue Lagoon
places.text: The Blue Lagoon lies about 15 km from Port Dickson town which provides a breathtaking view of the surrounding greenery and the blue open sea and having fun in the sun.

destinations.name: Cameron Highlands
destinations.intro: The Cameron Highlands are in Pahang, Peninsular Malaysia. It is approximately 85 km from Ipoh or about 200 km from Kuala Lumpur. The retreat has a diverse population of more than 43,000 people.
destinations.eat_notes: Food is not a problem at the Cameron Highlands. There are many Malay, Western, Indian and Chinese restaurants to pick and choose from. While you are here, do try the steamboat, a pot of boiling soup where you can cook your own meat and vegetables.
