places.name: Gunung (Mount) Brinchang
places.text: At 6,666 ft above sea level, this is the highest point in Malaysia which is accessible by car. At the top of the mountain is a radio and television station.

places.name: Mossy Forest
places.text: There is a boardwalk at the top of Gunung (Mount) Brinchang which takes you through the Mossy Forest. This reserve is unlike any other in peninsular Malaysia: its base is covered with a thick carpet of moss.

places.name: Parit Waterfall
places.text: Terrible view, all the river is full of rubbish. There are two ways to get to the waterfall: you could either start from the Forestry Department or take Trail 4 which is at the side of the Century Pines Resort.

places.name: Robinson Waterfall
places.text: The falls are a short distance from Tanah Rata. It can be reached via Path 9. (See section. #Stay Safe for trail 9.)

places.name: Boh Tea Centre and Sg Palas Plantation
places.text: Operated by Malaysia's largest tea company. Tours available of tea factory. Interactive educational studio, a retail outlet, and a nice cafe. Stunning vistas of rolling hills amidst a carefully tendered tea plantation.
places.address: follow the main road from Brinchang towards Kg Raja. After the Equatorial Hotel, look for

places.name: Cameron Bharat Tea Plantation
places.text: Second largest producer of tea in Malaysia. You can walk around the plantations and take photos. There is a cafe from where you can have a breathtaking view of the tea plantation.

places.name: Sam Poh Temple
places.text: If you are tired of hiking, Sam Poh is worth the visit. Built in 1972, it is the 4th largest Buddhist temple in the country.

places.name: Time Tunnel – The Local Museum
places.text: The Time Tunnel is Malaysia's first memorabilia "museum". It is recognised as one of the main attractions of the Cameron Highlands. The galleria is filled with objects de art that showcase what life was like in Malaysia after the Japanese occupation.
places.address: located within the Kok Lim Strawberry Farm

places.name: Malaysian Agriculture Research and Development Institute (MARDI)
places.text: Research and educational center. Mardi is home to 40 varieties of roses, 10 strawberries, 100 citrus fruits and exhibits a rich collection of hydroponic technique for agriculture.

places.name: Bertam Valley
places.text: The Ringlet to Sungai Koyan road is a particular picturesque mountain road, which starts with countless greenhouses and quickly changes into rainforest covered hills of immense beauty and colour, which form to be gradles for soft fog clouds being trapped among them.

places.name: Trail 1
places.text: The peak at 2,032 m, which can be reached by walking 'Trail 1' from Brinchang.
places.address: Finding the path can be a bit confusing as the sign is about 10 m from the main road. Ask

places.name: Trail 2
places.text: The trail merges later with Trail 3. Quite steep and not well indicated.
places.address: start in Brinchang at Sam Poh Buddhist Temple.

places.name: Trail 3: Gunung Berembun
places.text: The Gunung Berembun at 1,840 m is overgrown and offers little view over the valley. Still the trail is wide and clearly defined. It takes you through the jungle with a couple of stream crossings.
places.address: start at Arcadia Cottage near the golf course

places.name: Trail 4: Parit Waterfall
places.text: Easy and mostly paved trail to the Parit Waterfall, though as of May 2019 there were a few small fallen trees across the path. The river and the waterfall are nothing to write about except that they are filled with garbage.

places.name: Trail 5
places.text: Trail 5 merges with Trail 3 on the way up to Gunung Berembun or down to the golf course.
places.address: start at MARDI (Malaysian Agriculture Research and Development Institute)

places.name: Trail 6
places.text: There seem to be two different trails called Trail 6, both labeled as such on OpenStreetMap. The one on tourist maps runs between Bharat Tea Plantation and the summit of Gunung Jasar, but the maps themselves say it's not well marked.

places.name: Trail 7: Gunung Berembun
places.text: The first 300 m are very overgrown (watch out for ticks). Later the path widen and become very pleasant and well marked. The end is steep until it merges with trail 3 to the summit.
places.address: start at MARDI (Malaysian Agriculture Research and Development Institute)

places.name: Trail 8: Gunung Berembun
places.text: Very difficult trail (climb?) until it merges with trail 3 and 7 to the summit of Gunung Berembun.

places.name: Trail 9 and 9A: Bharat Plantations
places.text: This trail is not recommended as robberies have been reported in 2016 (stopped apparently in 2017?) See #Stay Safe for more information.

places.name: Trail 10: Gunung Jasar
places.text: Day hike. Takes you through an ancient mossy forest (~1½ hr to Jasar).
places.address: starts next to Tan's Camellia Garden, behind H2O Apartments and Highland Villa Resort

places.name: Trail 11
places.text: This trail was closed due to landslides in 2017, but it is open and fully walkable. It can be walked from beginning until the end, even though OsmAnd or Mapy.cz say you can’t.

places.name: Trail 13: Gunung Mentigi
places.text: It is closed for construction developments.

places.name: Trail 14: Gunung Irau
places.text: Gunung Irau is the highest peak of the Cameron Highlands. The trail takes you through the Mossy forest. Can be very challenging and muddy after rainfalls. The track has been closed since 7 Feb 2018 due to landslides.
places.address: starts at the end of the Mossy Forest boardwalk

places.name: Cameron Highlands Golf Course
places.text: This is a beautiful although quite challenging 18-hole course with tricky greens and terrain. Like most of Malaysia however, it could benefit from cleaning up some of the garbage in certain areas, such as the steams.

places.name: Open Air Market - Kea Farm
places.text: Well-known place to get fresh vegetables and fruits including strawberries and sweet corn.

places.name: Night Market (Pasar Malam)
places.text: Open on Friday and Saturday nights (open every day on holiday season and public holiday).
places.address: opposite the police station in Brinchang

places.name: Ee Feng Gu Honey Bee Farm
places.text: This farm has been around for ages. It is one of the best places to buy fresh honey.
places.address: 75, Batu 43, Green Cow, Kea Farm, Brinchang

places.name: Cactus Point
places.text: Situated on a hill slope, this establishment sells practically every type of cactus imaginable.

places.name: Cactus Valley
places.text: This nursery has one of the best collections of cactus in Malaysia. Some of the species here are more than 60 years old. There are no charges for photography at the nursery.

places.name: Rose Centre
places.text: More than a 100 varieties of roses are grown here. Aside from the abundance of the beautiful roses, is a lovely walk up the hillside on the property with excellent view of the surrounding area.
places.address: Located at Rose Valley Village, Kea Farm, Brinchang

places.name: Big Red Strawberry Farm
places.text: The Big Red Strawberry Farm is one of the largest Agro-Tourism Farms in Malaysia. Pick your own strawberries and tomatoes. The sheltered farm covers an area of approximately 5 hectares.

places.name: Kok Lim Self-Plucking Strawberry Farm
places.text: The Kok Lim Strawberry Farm is one of the largest strawberry farms at the retreat. The strawberries here are grown on "A-frames". This is a good place to get the best price for the strawberries you pluck.

places.name: Yung Seng Souvenir Shop
places.text: Art and craft store. An upmarket shop with an interesting mix of handicrafts and souvenirs of the Orang Asli.

places.name: Butterfly Garden and Butterfly Farm
places.text: The Butterfly Garden and Butterfly Farm are next to each other. Both have a shop at their top floors where you can purchase traditional handicrafts and fashion clothing.

places.name: Gerai Opah
places.text: If you're looking for a good filling breakfast, try the kampung nasi lemak. Only open for breakfast and until it runs out so hurry up
places.address: No.9, Gerai Makan Laluan Besar, Tanah Rata

places.name: Yong Teng Cafe
places.text: Run by the nicest old couple. There are deaf so all communications are by signs.

places.name: Jasmine's Cafe
places.text: Big on Dutch soccer clubs, there's only one color that characterises this place, Oranje. Superb ambience, good chicken chops and some vegetarian options.

places.name: Restoran Mayflower
places.text: Good place for steamboat and Chinese food.

places.name: Jungle Bar

stays.text: Located in the centre of Brinchang. Cheap and good.

stays.name: Cameronian Inn
stays.text: Cottage with a nice garden, afternoon tea and strawberry scones. Mix of dorms and private rooms. TV room with AstroTV.

stays.name: Kang Traveller's Lodge
stays.text: Very basic but pleasant dorm accommodation. Free hot showers, free 24 hr Wi-Fi, pool table and nightly bonfires. Movie room with DVDs available.

stays.name: Vintage Guesthouse

stays.name: Father's Guest House
stays.text: A popular holiday retreat. In-house cafe serves local and western cuisines. Big Wi-Fi lounge area. Tour and transport bookings available at reception counter.

stays.name: Sg Pauh Campsite
stays.text: The campsite has got all the basic amenities like washrooms, BBQ and cold showers. There are electrical sockets spread around the site.

stays.name: Tudor Home Inn
stays.text: Kopitiam serving local favorite food. Car parking available. Local information counter. Sightseeing tour arrangement. Close to the night market and a mosque's loudspeaker.

stays.name: Twin Pines

stays.name: Westwood Highland

stays.name: Hillview Inn

stays.name: Cameron Highlands Resort
stays.text: Probably the nicest place to stay in the Highlands, the Cameron Highlands Resort is built around a large 1930s colonial house with modern extensions.

stays.name: Century Pines Resort
stays.text: Tanah Rata. A cosy hotel located at the north-end of Tanah Rata. It houses a spa which offers spa and massage packages. There are 111 rooms in various sizes; superior, deluxe, suite.

stays.name: Hotel De' La Ferns
stays.text: Batu 39, Jalan Besar, Tanah Rata. It is the latest boutique hotel at the Cameron Highlands. The hotel is approximately 2 km from Tanah Rata.

stays.name: Strawberry Park Resort
stays.text: Tanah Rata. Neo Tudor-style resort contains 230 modern styled fully-furnished rooms and apartments that blend in with their natural surroundings.

stays.name: The Lakehouse
stays.text: Ringlet. Tudor style hotel sitting atop a hill and overlooking the Sultan Abu Bakar Lake near the town of Ringlet. Short drive from Tanah Rata.

destinations.name: Genting Highlands
destinations.intro: Genting Highlands is in Pahang, Malaysia which is famous for having Malaysia's only legal casinos, as well as theme parks, shopping malls and hotels.
destinations.eat_notes: There are countless options for dining in Genting Highlands, from choices of local food, fast food to fine dining experience of cuisine from all over the world. Being in a tourist resort, prices are generally higher than elsewhere in Malaysia, but there are always cheaper options available around.

notes.title: School holidays
notes.text: Late May to June and most of December are school holidays: book early, and expect traffic and queues at anything family-friendly.

notes.title: Hari Raya Aidilfitri
notes.text: The biggest holiday of the year. Cities empty out, highways jam with people heading home, and many eateries close for the first few days. The date moves about 11 days earlier every year.

places.name: Chin Swee Caves Temple
places.text: A grand religious site located on a sharp, rocky slope near the peak of Resorts World Genting. Embark on a cultural journey through a visual depiction of the afterlife, or simply enjoy the magnificent mountainous landscape from the temple.
places.address: take Awana Skyway and alight at Chin Swee Station

places.name: Cradle Rock
places.text: Located along the road side along the road up to Resorts World Genting, this special large rock has been standing in a perfect balance on top of other rocks below.

places.name: Genting Strawberry Leisure Farms
places.text: The farm consists of strawberry farm, lavender garden, hydrangea garden and mushroom farm.
places.address: No. 1, Lot 3707, Jalan Jati 2, Gohtong Jaya

places.name: Happy Bee Farm, Insect World and Butterfly Wonderland
places.text: Enjoy the natural goodness of honey cultivated in the farm; view a vast collection of unique and weird insects from all corners of the earth and also to feast your eyes on a beautiful spectrum of dancing colours as butterflies of species from all over the…

places.name: SkySymphony

places.name: Talking Garden
places.text: A small outdoor garden behind Genting SkyWorlds Hotel facing down towards Kuala Lumpur.

places.name: Tan Sri (Dr) Lim Goh Tong Memorial Hall
places.text: The memorial park for the founder of Tan Sri Lim Goh Tong Resorts World Genting and Genting Berhad. The memorial hall features a wooden effigy of Lim surrounded by orchid blossoms with a mural of Resorts World Genting in the background.

places.name: Genting Casino
places.text: It also houses the Genting Club for Genting Rewards Gold and above members.

places.name: SkyCasino
places.text: The main casino area spans over two floors on 1st and 2nd floor. The 3rd floor houses the SkyCasino Premium Gaming for Crockfords Platinum Club and SkyCasino Gold Club members.

places.name: Arena of Stars

places.name: Bona Cinemas
places.text: This only theatre in Genting Highlands features an IMAX cinema.

places.name: Genting International Convention Centre
places.text: Convention centre with various halls capable of hosting events, concerts and performances for up to 2,000 people.

places.name: Genting International Showroom
places.text: Show and concert venue with weekly performances from various shows and artists. It has a capacity of 1,000 seats.

places.name: Genting SkyWorlds Theme Park
places.text: features various themed rides, suitable for adults and children. It spans over the following themed section areas: Studio Plaza, Eagle Mountain, Central Park, Rio, Andromeda Base, Liberty Lane, Epic, Robots Rivet Town and Ice Age.

places.name: Skytropolis Indoor Theme Park
places.text: Indoor theme park located inside First World Plaza. Spans over around 4 hectares and has more than 20 rides.

places.name: Awana Bio Park
places.text: Explore the virgin jungle of Genting Highlands through jungle trekking which are divided into three trails: biodiversity trail (2.7 km), conservation trail (800 m) and herb forest trail (1.7 km).

places.name: Awana Genting Highlands Golf Course
places.text: 18-hole golf course surrounded by lush greens and year-long crisp mountain breeze.

places.name: Gohtong Sports Centre

places.name: Ripley's Believe It Or Not! Adventureland

places.text: Cross the boundaries of time, distance and physical limitations with cutting-edge virtual reality technology. Step into new worlds where you can do all the things you’ve never thought you could.

places.address: go up one floor (by lift or escalator) from First World Hotel lobby

places.text: This 4-story shopping mall features the SkyCasino and the upper station of Awana Skyway. It features the SkySymphony colorful hanging balls orchestra.

places.name: Genting Grand Complex

places.text: This shopping mall houses more than 20 dining, retail and service outlets. It is connected to Genting Highlands Premium Outlets by two link bridges. It houses the Awana Transport Hub at level 1 and Awana Station of Awana SkyWay at level 4.

places.name: Genting Highlands Premium Outlets
places.text: An outlet with various choices of designer fashions and sportswear, fine leather and luggage, houseware and home furnishings, accessories and jewelry, gifts and special items and shoes.

places.name: AYU Awana
places.text: The restaurant and poolside lounge which showcases a special smokehouse and grill menu, regional dishes, healthy delights and an extensive cocktail list for both sun-kissed afternoons and moonlit dinners.

destinations.name: Tioman
destinations.intro: Tioman (Malay: Pulau Tioman, "Tioman Island") is a small island, 20 km long and 12 km wide, off the east coast of peninsular Malaysia. In the 1970s, Time magazine selected Tioman as one of the world's most beautiful islands. The densely forested island is still sparsely inhabited.
destinations.eat_notes: Depending on where you eat, food can be quite expensive on Tioman, compared to other places in Malaysia. "Street food" in the form of fried rice or burger booths can be found everywhere, but opening times vary. During Ramadan, most of the restaurants around the island are closed for lunch.

places.name: B&J Dive Center
places.text: Has two full-service dive shops, at Air Batang and Salang. A very accommodating bunch of people with good dives. B&J can cater to technical divers offering nitrox and trimix as well as deeper wreck expeditions.

places.name: Blue Heaven Divers
places.text: Small, friendly dive centre. Blue Heaven Divers can also help you to arrange your accommodation.

places.name: Eco Divers
places.text: A small diving centre with limited equipment and good diving courses.

places.name: Ray’s Dive Adventure
places.text: Dive with local guided Shamrock to explore underwater world. With friendly and helpful staff and have experienced divers. Provides accommodation too for divers.

places.name: Tioman Dive Centre
places.text: Enjoy diving in clear blue waters over beautiful coral reefs teeming with marine life. Tioman is perfect for both learning to dive (TDC offer a comprehensive range of PADI dive training courses) and diving for fun at over 20 dive sites.

places.name: Scuba Do Dive Centre
places.text: provides scuba diving courses including Open Water, Advanced Open Water, Nitrox, Rescue, Divemaster and Instructor.

places.name: Beach Shack Surf
places.text: Located in front of the Juara beach, this is one of the oldest surf centres on the island.

places.name: Tekek – Juara jungle trek
places.text: In front of the power station closed doors, you will see a discreet "to Juara" sign on your right. Go around the power station fence on an uncleared path and spot the red and white plastic stripes knotted to the trees that mark the track.
places.address: from the Tekek jetty, turn left (north) and follow the road till you see a "to Juara" sign

places.text: To reach the waterfalls, just follow a marked path for about 30 min. The path starts at the south beach, next to the turtle breeding farm. Opposite of the great rocks, which lie on the beach.

stays.text: Located at a very small kampong about 200 m north of Air Batang and the second last ferry stop.

stays.text: Kampung Paya (south of Tekek). A typical Tioman resort featuring an almost-private beach, a particularly good restaurant, a swimming pool, a dive shop, spa experience and chalets of varying standards.

destinations.name: Putrajaya
destinations.intro: Putrajaya, an "Intelligent Garden City" and the federal administrative capital of Malaysia, is a showcase city under construction some 30 km south of the capital Kuala Lumpur. To the west is Putrajaya's adjacent sister city, Cyberjaya, which is built along the same lines and is aimed at attracting the IT industry.

places.text: Pretty in pink, this mosque has a capacity of 15,000 worshippers and its 116-meter minaret is the tallest in Southeast Asia. Non-Muslims may not enter the mosque building itself during prayer hours.

places.name: Putrajaya International Convention Centre
places.text: Presint 5. At the end of the Putrajaya Boulevard, this showcase squashed UFO of a building, designed to resemble a Malay belt buckle, was built for the Organization of Islamic Countries conference in 2003.

places.name: Seri Perdana
places.text: Enormous official residence of the Prime Minister of Malaysia. Has been open to visitors in the past, but as of 2009 is closed to the public.

places.name: Taman Putra Perdana
places.text: Pleasantly landscaped (and usually very quiet) hilltop park connecting the Shangri-La towards the Putra Perdana building, with some of the best views in town.

places.name: Millennium Monument
places.text: 68-m pillar in the shape of a hibiscus flower, with a walkway around it documenting the history of Malaysia.

places.name: Botanical Gardens
places.text: The Botanical Gardens has been designed as an Arcadia or a national sanctuary for the Malaysian living collection of plant taxonomy as well as a centre for education and research.

places.name: Taman Ekuestrian Putrajaya
places.text: The Sport and Recreational Precinct of Putrajaya, this equestrian centre takes advantage of the 70 acres of lush greenery to provide an attractive location and facilities for riders to experience a new environment and sporting background for equestrian competitions.

places.name: Alamanda
places.text: As indicated by the logo, alamanda is a type of flower commonly found in Malaysia, Putrajaya's premier shopping center.

places.name: Medan Selera P8
places.text: An open air and spacious food court catering to the residents of the community and government staff offering mostly local dishes at a fairly cheap price. You can also try the western menu at Harris's Bistro on the upper level of the food court.

places.name: Taman Warisan
places.text: An agro-based food stop where you can dine and shop for fresh fruits at the same place.

places.name: Night Market
places.text: Every Tuesday and Friday there is a nice night market with aisles of fresh foods, prepared foods, and household goods. Like Putrajaya itself, it is slightly less multi-cultural than many Malaysian night markets.

stays.text: Despite the faintly ridiculous name, this is a well-regarded resort-style spa hotel in neighboring Cyberjaya.

stays.name: Palm Garden Hotel
stays.text: Formerly Renaissance, also in the IOI Resort, is a slightly more humanely sized hotel and probably a better choice than the Marriott.

destinations.name: George Town
destinations.intro: George Town is the capital city of the Malaysian state of Penang. It is Malaysia's sixth largest city, with a population of about 708,000, with 1.7 million in the metro area, as of 2020. Founded as an entrepôt in 1786, it was the first British settlement in Southeast Asia.
destinations.eat_notes: Penang is widely considered to be the food capital of Malaysia, and George Town is the best place in Penang to eat. (See Penang for listings of local dishes.) Gurney Drive may be the main location where tourists go to have their food, but that does not necessarily mean that the best food can be found there.

notes.title: School holidays
notes.text: Late May to June and most of December are school holidays: book early, and expect traffic and queues at anything family-friendly.

notes.title: Hari Raya Aidilfitri
notes.text: The biggest holiday of the year. Cities empty out, highways jam with people heading home, and many eateries close for the first few days. The date moves about 11 days earlier every year.

notes.title: Chinese New Year
notes.text: Lanterns, lion dances and open houses. Many Chinese-run shops and eateries close for the first two or three days, so plan your meals.

notes.title: Thaipusam
notes.text: One of the great Hindu processions in the world, at Batu Caves and in George Town. Unforgettable, and extremely crowded.

notes.title: Deepavali
notes.text: Little India streets are lit up and busy with sweets and shopping in the weeks before.

notes.title: George Town Festival
notes.text: A month of art, theatre and street events around George Town's heritage day on 7 July.

notes.title: Durian season
notes.text: The main durian season. Roadside stalls and orchards are at their best - Balik Pulau, Raub and Bentong are the names to know.

places.name: Armenian Street
places.text: Armenian Street, once home to some of the city's prominent Armenian merchants is now one of the hippest streets, with a number of interesting crafts shops, temples, at least two museums and probably most importantly, Zacharevic's street art of the two kids on a bicycle.

places.name: Gurney Drive
places.text: This seafront street and promenade now forms part of George Town's Central Business District (CBD). Home to upscale shopping malls, an eponymous hawker centre and towering skyscrapers, it is also a good place to unwind and stroll along.
places.address: Enter from the intersection of Kelawei Road, Jalan Bagan Jermal and Jalan Tanjung Tokong

places.name: Little India
places.text: Covering an area around Queen Street, Chulia Street and Market Street, Little India is an ethnic Indian enclave. Walking on the streets, you cannot avoid smelling Indian spices and hearing Bollywood music.

places.name: Penang Hill
places.text: At above sea level, the peak of Penang Hill offers a panoramic bird's eye view of the city and fresher air. For more details, refer to Air Itam#See.

places.name: Penang Botanic Gardens
places.text: The gardens were established by Charles Curtis way back in 1884; it's generally known as the Waterfall Gardens by the locals because of a waterfall within it.

places.name: Entopia Butterfly Farm
places.text: Home to some 13,000 species of butterflies, the Entopia Butterfly Farm also contains numerous other invertebrates and insects.

places.name: Tropical Spice Garden
places.text: An eight-acre collection of secondary jungle filled with various types of spices that are in common use in the kitchens of Penang.

places.name: Penang National Park
places.text: This small national park contains easy walking trails in the jungle. Along the way you will see white sandy beaches, monkeys and a light house, all while spending up to half the day in the jungles far from the noise of the city.

places.name: Padang Kota Lama
places.text: It was planted by the British as the main cricket ground for the Penang Cricket Club, which moved to new premises in 1939 and was re-named the Penang Sports Club in 1947.

places.name: Penang Sports Club
places.text: It was founded as the Penang Cricket Club in 1900. It moved to its current location in 1939, and assumed its current name in 1947.

places.name: Protestant Cemetery
places.text: The burial site of early European administrators and merchants, including Captain Francis Light, Thomas Leonowens and Michael Arratoon Anthony. Filled with crumbling, vegetation-covered tombs, it bears witness to a century of colonisation.

places.name: Jewish Cemetery
places.text: The cemetery that once served Penang's Jewish community, and one of the few reminders of a once-thriving community during the colonial period. The Jewish community no longer exists, the last member having died in 2011.

places.name: Campbell Street Market
places.text: One of the oldest markets in George Town, dates back to 1900.

places.name: Fort Cornwallis
places.text: The fort, named for Charles Cornwallis, is built on the site where Francis Light, founder of Penang, landed on 11 August 1786. It was first built in 1793. But this site was an unlikely spot to defend the city from invasion.

places.name: City Hall
places.text: The headquarters of the Penang Island City Council, the local government of George Town. A well-preserved colonial building constructed in 1903 when Penang was a British crown colony.

places.name: Penang State Assembly Building
places.text: Built in the mid-19th century as part of the Central Police Station, this Anglo-Indian Classical building became the State Assembly building in 1963. The building is closed to the public; tourists can only view it from the outside.

places.name: High Court of Penang
places.text: Inaugurated in 1903, this Palladian-style building now houses the High Court of Penang, which had been established in 1809 as the first judiciary in modern Malaysia.

places.name: Wisma Kastam
places.text: This colonial building houses the Penang branch of the Royal Malaysian Customs. It was completed in 1907 as a Malayan Railway station. As it is not beside a rail track, it was known as the only rail station in the world without a railway.

places.name: Queen Victoria Memorial Clock Tower
places.text: The high clock tower was presented by local millionaire Cheah Chen Eok in 1897 to commemorate the Diamond Jubilee of Queen Victoria.

places.name: Beach Street
places.text: As the main Central Business District (CBD) of George Town, Beach Street is lined with mercantile buildings constructed between the 1880s and the 1950s.

places.name: Wisma Yeap Chor Ee
places.text: An elegant colonial building built in the 1920s, it once belonged to Yeap Chor Ee, a China-born tycoon. The building now houses @CAT, a coworking space popular amongst startups and freelancers.

places.name: Penang State Museum
places.text: Formerly the Penang Free School which was built in two separate stages in 1896 and 1906. The museum is an interesting starting point to discover the multi-ethnic background of George Town.

places.name: Sun Yat-sen Museum
places.text: The Sun Yat Sen Museum is a beautifully preserved house museum and one of the smallest museums in Asia.

places.name: Made in Penang Interactive Museum
places.text: Housed within the Behn-Meyer Building which was built in the late 19th century, this interactive museum features various three-dimensional interactive art pieces that depict Penang's culture, history and lifestyle.

places.name: Penang Time Tunnel Museum
places.text: An interactive museum that features three-dimensional artwork about Penang's history.
places.hours: Mon-Fri 9:15AM-6PM; Sat Sun and public holidays: 9:15AM-6:30PM

places.name: The Roman Catholic Museum Diocese of Penang
places.text: The ground floor presents the origin of Catholicism in the Far East in general and in Penang in particular. It also informs about the activities of the diocese of Penang and the ethnic makeup of its members.

places.name: Asia Camera Museum
places.text: A lot of antique cameras and photographic accessories.

places.name: Cheong Fatt Tze Mansion
places.text: Built in the 1890s, and restored in the 1990s (earning it a UNESCO award in 2000), this indigo-blue Chinese mansion was the main residence of Cheong Fatt Tze (called Zhang Bishi in China), known as the Rockefeller of the East and J.P.
places.hours: Guided tours are available at 11AM and 2PM. Each tour lasts 45 minutes.

places.name: Pinang Peranakan Mansion
places.text: Built as the home of Kapitan Chung Keng Kwee, a prominent Chinese tycoon, this green-coloured Straits Eclectic house is now home to thousands of Peranakan antiques once used by the Peranakans.

places.name: Chinese Clan Jetties
places.text: There are six clan jetties along the eastern coastline of George Town. They are worth walking to and looking at, as they provide an insight to the way local Chinese live in traditional huts built on the sea on stilts.

places.name: Leong San Tong Khoo Kongsi
places.text: Built in 1850 by the forefathers of Khoo family who emigrated from China as a clan-house for members of the Khoo family. In 1836, construction of a new temple began and was completed eight years later.

places.name: St. George's Church
places.text: The oldest Anglican church in Southeast Asia was completed in 1818. The church was designed by Robert Smith, a military engineer who is known for his oil paintings of early Penang, which are now housed within the Penang State Museum.

places.name: Goddess of Mercy Temple
places.text: Built in 1801, the Goddess of Mercy Temple is one of the oldest Chinese temples in Penang. This Taoist temple is flocked to by pilgrims year round, particularly on the 1st and 15th days of each lunar month.

places.name: Sri Mariamman Temple
places.text: Built in 1833 and expanded in 1933, the Sri Mariamman Temple is the oldest Hindu temple in Penang. It is dedicated to the deity Sri Muthu Mariamman and features a gopuram (sculptured tower) of 38 Hindu deities.

places.name: Kapitan Keling Mosque
places.text: Built in 1803 and named after Caudeer Mohudeen, an Indian Muslim merchant who was also the Kapitan Keling, or leader of the Indian Muslim community.

places.name: Church of the Assumption
places.text: The first permanent Catholic church to be built in George Town, the Church of the Assumption was established by a group of Eurasian immigrants who accompanied Captain Francis Light to Penang.

places.name: Wat Chayamangalaram
places.text: Founded in 1845, this Thai-style Buddhist temple is famous for its reclining Buddha, one of the world's longest.

places.name: Dhammikarama Burmese Temple
places.text: A Burmese Buddhist temple founded in 1803. At the entrance a pair of white elephants, which are sacred in Buddhism, guard the temple while within, a bodhi tree and wishing pond greets the visitor.

places.name: Arulmigu Balathandayuthapani Temple
places.text: Located at a hilltop next to the Penang Botanic Gardens, the Arulmigu Balathandayuthapani Temple was built in the mid-19th century, making it one of the oldest Hindu temples in George Town.

places.name: Han Jiang Ancestral Temple
places.text: A temple built in 1864 by the Teochew community.

places.name: Benggali Mosque
places.text: It was built in 1803, and rebuilt in 1958 on the same address. It serves Indian-Muslims from Bengal.

places.name: Rainbow Skywalk
places.text: This glass walkway above sea level is not for the acrophobic. Opened in 2016, the Rainbow Skywalk, at the top of the KOMTAR Tower, is the highest glass skywalk in Malaysia.
places.hours: Sun-Thu 11AM-10PM, Fri Sat 11AM-11PM, school and public holidays: 10AM-11PM

places.name: The Gravityz
places.text: Launched in 2018, The Gravityz is a series of rope courses along the outside of KOMTAR Tower. Again not for the acrophobic, it includes a flying fox zipline and a narrow mesh-wire pathway designed to challenge your balancing skills.

places.name: Occupy Beach Street
places.text: Every Sunday morning, Beach Street, Bishop Street, Church Street and Church Street Ghaut are turned into car-free zones. Family-friendly recreational activities and roadside stalls will be set up along these roads.

places.name: Hin Bus Art Depot
places.text: Art aficionadi can head to this art gallery, which periodically curates art exhibitions. It also contains open spaces for events, a garden and cafes. A pop-up market featuring local artists and other retailers is held every Sunday.

places.name: Penang Bowl
places.text: A 16-lane bowling venue for bowlers within the city centre.

places.name: The Habitat
places.text: The Habitat offers well-constructed jungle trails. The Curtis Crest Tree Top Walk is an elevated semi-circular platform, the highest of its kind in Penang - providing an all-round bird's eye view of Penang Hill out to the vast expanse of the Malacca Straits.

places.name: ESCAPE Theme Park
places.text: The ESCAPE Theme Park consists of two parts - one for jungle-themed activities and another for aquatic games.

places.name: Penang Sports Club
places.text: It was founded as the Penang Cricket Club in 1900 at what is today the Padang Kota Lama, which was its original cricket ground. It moved to its current premises in 1939, and assumed its current name in 1947.

places.name: Batu Ferringhi
places.text: The sandy beaches of Batu Ferringhi also offer various activities, ranging from parasailing to riding a beach buggy.

places.name: Paintball at Penang War Museum
places.text: What better way to enjoy a paintball match than a historical setting at a former British fortress? Packages are available for groups of 10 to 20.

places.name: Chowrasta Market
places.text: Built in 1890, Chowrasta Market is one of the oldest wet markets in Malaysia.

places.name: Lorong Kulit Flea Market
places.text: Said to be the biggest flea market in Penang, the open-air Lorong Kulit Flea Market is sited right outside the City Stadium. All sorts of second-hand goods, imitation products, eclectic items and even antiques can be found here at bargain prices.

places.name: Batu Ferringhi Night Market
places.text: One of the most well-known night markets in Penang. For more details, refer to Batu Ferringhi#Buy.

places.name: Balik Pulau Night Market
places.text: For more details, refer to Balik Pulau#Buy.

places.name: 1st Avenue
places.text: Next to Komtar and Prangin Mall. This stylish downtown mall contains a 5D cineplex, as well as a karaoke. Several shoplots selling electronic goods and various sorts of apparel.

places.name: All Seasons Place
places.text: Anchored by Giant hypermarket, the first strip mall in Penang houses several dining outlets, as well as localised stores selling knock-off goods.

places.name: Gurney Paragon
places.text: Built around a colonial-era school building, this upmarket shopping mall contains an IMAX-equipped cineplex, as well as a wide variety of al fresco restaurants and apparel shops.

places.name: Gurney Plaza
places.text: One of Penang's premier shopping malls, the mall contains various entertainment options, such as a 12-screen cineplex, a karaoke, a laser tag outlet and an escape games venue.

places.name: Penang Time Square
places.text: This shopping mall contains more localised retail stores offering anything from apparel to pedicure. It is also well-known for its nightclubs and dance clubs in its basement.

places.name: Prangin Mall
places.text: Catering to the lower- and middle-class residents, the mall contains several localised retail stores. Get all sorts of apparel and electronic goods, including laptops and smartphones, at lower prices here.

places.name: Queensbay Mall
places.text: Penang's largest mall contains a wide variety of entertainment options, including a cineplex, a karaoke, a laser tag outlet and an escape games venue. A strong contender to Gurney Plaza with numerous international brands.

places.name: Straits Quay
places.text: Upmarket seaside shopping mall next to a marina, with British-style architecture. Al fresco restaurants line the ground floor. The mall also contains a Royal Selangor pewter outlet, a convention centre and PenangPac, a performing arts venue.
places.address: Jalan Seri Tanjung Pinang, Tanjung Tokong

places.name: Udini Square
places.text: The mall is well-known for stores offering hardware and sports equipment. It is also opposite a Tesco hypermarket, convenient for shoppers on a budget.

places.name: Ghee Hiang Bakery
places.text: The oldest bakery in Penang, established since 1856; other well-known products include sesame seed oil.

places.name: Him Heang Bakery
places.text: This may be the most famous Chinese bakery in Penang, popular among locals and Singaporean tourists. Its most famous products are Tambun Pneah and Beh Teh Sor.

places.name: Ng Kee Cake Shop
places.text: The shop produces and sells Cantonese traditional biscuits including wedding biscuits. One of the famous biscuits is pepper biscuit (咸切酥, Ham Chit Soo).

places.name: Sin Hock Seng Bakery
places.text: (新福成) The shop sells more than one hundred different types of biscuit. Basically, you can find any kind of traditional biscuit there.

places.name: EE Beng Vegetarian Food
places.text: It's a small self-serve buffet style vegetarian restaurant. Good choice of food at an easy on the wallet price.
places.address: On Lebuh Dickens. (Dickens Street)(Near the junction of Penang Road)

places.name: Sri Wangi Selera Ibunda
places.text: Serving Sri Lankan and western food. Also home to the Penang Hash House Harriers chapter. In the later-earlier hours it becomes a bar and place where the regulars and travellers hang out.

places.name: Red Garden Cafe
places.text: Local food: satay, roasted and BBQ'd chicken, duck and pork variations with noodles or rice (Chinese stall in the right corner). Also Thai, Filipino, western and fusion food.

places.name: New World Park Food City
places.text: Local specialities including curry mee, prawn mee, laksa, chee cheong and fun. For dessert try the ais kacang special with ice cream on top.

places.name: Ban Heang
places.text: Outlet opened in Nov 2014 of the locally famous biscuit and delicacy manufacturer. Also sells organic ice creams, sorbets and dried fruit. Its own restaurant linked next door is cheap and cheerful with a wide variety of fresh local and western-style foods.

places.name: Krsna Restaurant
places.text: Cheap banana leaf-style food but now served on paper. Loads of rice with dal and condiments.
places.address: In the heart of Little India

places.name: Kapitan's
places.text: No matter what time of the day, this mamak restaurant serves up great Indian food at a decent price. They are well known for their biryani, tandoori chicken and butter chicken.

places.name: Tai Tong
places.text: Well-priced dim sum breakfasts, served in the traditional way on carts wheeled among the tables. Get there earlier for more variety.

places.name: No Eyed Deer Restaurant
places.text: Favourite haunt among the locals & expatriates living in Penang. Western and Asian cuisine, famous for its Laotian laksa, chicken parmigiana and steaks.
places.address: 98-1-26 Prima Tanjung, Jalan Fettes 11200 Tanjung Tokong

places.name: Seoul Garden Korean Restaurant
places.text: Long established venue that attracts Korean expatriates during lunch and dinner. Nice views.

places.name: Restaurant Au Jardin
places.text: One of only four Michelin-starred restaurants in Malaysia. Chef Kim Hock Su presents Malaysian ingredients, flavours, and stories with a steady hand, through the lens of fine French culinary technique.
places.address: The Warehouse @ Hin Bus Depot 125, Jalan Timah, 10150, Georgetown, Penang, Malaysia

places.name: The Garage
places.text: Once owned by the Wearne Brothers, the Garage used to be a motorcar showroom and has since been restored to its Art Deco glory, housing clubs, bars and boutiques.

places.name: MOIS Dance Club
places.text: A club for the younger crowd in a grand colonial-style building.

places.name: Soho Freehouse
places.text: Selection of continental food and beer. Good place for gaming with pool tables and foosball.

places.name: Hong Kong Bar
places.text: Famous and historically significant bar, home to many Commonwealth soldiers in Penang, particularly Australian forces based across the water at Butterworth.

places.name: Starbucks Signing Store
places.text: Opened in November 2019, this is the 4th Starbucks signing store in the world.

stays.name: Hang Chow Hotel
stays.text: Budget hotel with free Wi-Fi. Family room comes with a king and a queen bed, ceiling fan, air con and shower closet. The toilets are shared but very clean.

stays.name: Hotel Noble
stays.text: fan single and double rooms with bathrooms. Pay for Wi-Fi.

stays.name: Jim's Place
stays.text: Just look out for the reggae colours. Rooms about the same price as in other places. Friendly and helpful owner and staff.

stays.name: Mansion One Suites
stays.text: Available for daily, weekly and monthly rental.

stays.name: New Asia Hotel (Heritage)
stays.text: Heritage hotel, operated since World War II. A/C or fan), Wi-Fi, flat-screen TV, water jug/heater, spacious common dining area, clean, security CCTV, friendly staff.

stays.name: Old Penang Guesthouse (seems definitely closed)
stays.text: Budget heritage hostel with a modern fit-out in a historic restored pre-war building. Wi-Fi, In-room air-conditioning, towels and simple breakfast are included.

stays.name: Pin Seng Hotel
stays.text: fan single and double rooms with bathrooms has Wifi.

stays.name: Sim CityStay
stays.text: Clean, well organised and friendly. Free Wi-Fi.

stays.name: Star Lodge
stays.text: 39 Jl. Muntri. All rooms with windows, fan, sink, toilet and hot shower. Free 1-hr internet included in the room rate plus free Wi-Fi 24/7.

stays.name: Tune Hotel
stays.text: A/C and other services are not included in the online price, but can be purchased separately.

stays.name: Hotel Malaysia
stays.text: 3-star hotel with budget rates.

stays.name: Sunway Hotel Georgetown
stays.text: Walking distance to Komtar and famous New Lane hawker centre (night time). May ask for room without breakfast since there are many food stalls around the area.

stays.name: Hotel Penaga
stays.text: Rooms and suites individually furnished with antique cabinets, benches and chairs. The classics of mid-20th-century furniture design are also in every room.

stays.name: Cheong Fatt Tze Mansion
stays.text: Instead of just visiting this beautifully restored heritage building, why not consider sleeping there. The Mansion boasts 16 rooms with all the usual modern fittings.

stays.name: Eastern & Oriental Hotel Penang
stays.text: Founded in 1884 by the Sarkies brothers, legendary hoteliers who also founded Yangon's Strand Hotel and Singapore's famous Raffles Hotel, the E&O is Penang's grand old colonial hotel.

stays.name: G Hotel
stays.text: 168A Gurney Drive. Brand new post-modern luxury hotel in town with direct sea views. Comfortable, hip and funky.

destinations.name: Air Itam
destinations.intro: Air Itam (also spelt Ayer Itam or Air Hitam), is a town in central Penang Island (Pulau Pinang). Located west of George Town, Air Itam is largely a suburban area home to the famous Penang Hill, or Bukit Bendera, and the gigantic Kek Lok Si Temple.

notes.title: School holidays
notes.text: Late May to June and most of December are school holidays: book early, and expect traffic and queues at anything family-friendly.

notes.title: Hari Raya Aidilfitri
notes.text: The biggest holiday of the year. Cities empty out, highways jam with people heading home, and many eateries close for the first few days. The date moves about 11 days earlier every year.

notes.title: Chinese New Year
notes.text: Lanterns, lion dances and open houses. Many Chinese-run shops and eateries close for the first two or three days, so plan your meals.

notes.title: Thaipusam
notes.text: One of the great Hindu processions in the world, at Batu Caves and in George Town. Unforgettable, and extremely crowded.

notes.title: Deepavali
notes.text: Little India streets are lit up and busy with sweets and shopping in the weeks before.

places.name: Air Itam Dam
places.text: This was the first dam to be built on the island and is popular with locals as a picnic spot and jogging. The views of George Town at the crest of the dam are spectacular and rival Penang Hill.

places.name: Jade Emperor's Pavilion
places.text: A Taoist temple located near the foot of Penang Hill dedicated to the Jade Emperor, one of the most important figures in Taoism. The current temple dates back to 1905, with a former temple existing on the grounds since 1869.

places.name: Kek Lok Si Temple
places.text: An impressive and expansive hillside temple complex, reputed to be the largest Buddhist temple in South-east Asia. Much of the temple is free and you could easily spend a few hours exploring the halls and shrines.
places.address: 1 Tokong Kek Lok Si, off Jl Balik Pulau

places.name: Penang Hill Mosque
places.text: A simple but ornate mosque located at the top of Penang Hill.

places.name: Sri Aruloli Thirumurugan Temple
places.text: A small Hindu temple that is also one of the oldest in Penang.

places.name: War Memorial Park
places.text: A small park that is dedicated to the fallen of World War II.
places.address: Cnr Jl Bukit Bendera & Jl Paya Terubong

places.name: Penang Hill
places.text: A hill station established by the British, arguably the best views of George Town and the Malacca Strait can be found here, especially at night. Most people take the funicular rail to the top of the hill.
places.hours: Ticket counter hours: Mon-Fri 06:30-21:00, Sat Sun 06:30-22:00 (Last train to ba

places.name: Air Itam Market
places.text: The main market within Air Itam, selling almost fresh produce, clothing and other products. The market spills out beyond the main market building and runs along Jl Air Itam.
places.address: Cnr Jl Pasar and Jl Air Itam

places.name: Astaka Bukit Bendera
places.text: A modern multi-storey hawker centre located at the top of Penang Hill. The hawkers sell some decent local cuisine that you typically see around Penang, with a slight inflation on the price.
places.address: Penang Hill Complex, Jl Stesen Bukit Bendera

places.name: David Brown's Restaurant & Tea Terrace
places.text: Set in a British colonial building at the peak of Penang Hill, with colonial decor to match. They serve up Western food including steaks, hearty stews and roasts.

places.name: Pasar Air Itam Laksa
places.text: A simple and popular hawker at the local market selling one item, Assam Laksa. This particular stall was popularised by a visit from Anthony Bourdain. If you like your food a little spicy be sure to request chilli.

places.name: Sister's Curry Mee
places.text: A hawker stall that is popular among locals and run by two elderly sisters, selling Curry Mee.

places.name: OldTown White Coffee
places.text: A coffee shop/malaysian cafe on the map near the centre. No traveller has written it up yet, so go by the crowd.

destinations.name: Batu Ferringhi
destinations.intro: Batu Ferringhi is a beach town in Penang, Malaysia. It takes up the northern coast of Penang island along with the nearby beach town of Tanjung Bungah and the local fishing village of Teluk Bahang, which are also covered on this page.
destinations.eat_notes: There are plenty of places to eat all around, although discerning gourmands might want to explore less watered-down Malaysian cuisine in George Town. One option worth a special trip are the seafood restaurants at the pier of Teluk Bahang, at the northwestern tip of the island, past the hotels and the little village.

destinations.name: Butterworth
destinations.intro: Butterworth is the main town on the mainland side of Penang state in Malaysia. It was named after William John Butterworth, governor of the Straits Settlements from 1843-1855. Smaller, more industrial and practical, Butterworth does not have any of the atmosphere which George Town across the Penang Straits has.

destinations.name: Balik Pulau
destinations.intro: Balik Pulau (Malay: Back Island) is a town in Penang, Malaysia. Along with the surrounding area, Balik Pulau literally makes up the backcountry of the island, offering a laidback kampung lifestyle, with rice paddies and fruit farms scattered throughout, separated from Penang's main urban area by hills.

places.name: Saanen Dairy Goat Farm
places.text: Billy goats, nanny goats and kids in a raised and shaded enclosure. Clean with no overpowering smell. Free grass is provided to hand feed them and get as close as you want to pat their backs.

places.name: Titi Kerawang Waterfalls

places.name: Tropical Fruit Farm

places.name: Xuan Wu Temple

destinations.name: Ipoh
destinations.intro: Nestled within steep limestone hills on the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia, Ipoh has the proud heritage of a former tin mining boom town. While the current state capital of Perak had bigger heydays during the early 20th century, it is now better known amongst Malaysians for its excellent restaurants, hawkers, and famous local dishes.
destinations.eat_notes: When tin mining died out, food sustained Ipoh and made the city bustle once more. Like everywhere in Malaysia, the local food is dirt cheap and sublime. Loads of people come from all over just to fill their bellies, creating a headache of congestion during weekends.

notes.title: School holidays
notes.text: Late May to June and most of December are school holidays: book early, and expect traffic and queues at anything family-friendly.

places.name: Birch Memorial Clocktower
places.text: Dedicated to the first British Resident Minister of Perak who was murdered by a local Malay chief. The chief's profitable trade in Orang Asli, indigenous tribal folk, was curtailed by the British abolition of slavery.

places.name: Ipoh Railway Station
places.text: One of the three grand British-built stations on the former Malayan network. ETS trains connect this station, fondly dubbed "Taj Mahal of Ipoh", to KL's colonial beauty, Kuala Lumpur Railway Station (one stop before KL Sentral).

places.name: Ipoh Town Hall and Law Courts
places.text: The two buildings opposite the Railway Station, in neoclassical style.

places.name: Muzium Darul Ridzuan
places.text: An interesting historical museum of Perak in a former tin-mining tycoon's pretty mansion.

places.name: Padang Ipoh
places.text: This immaculate lawn near Jalan S.P. Seenivasagam was planted by the British during the colonial period as the cricket ground for the Ipoh Club, then a whites-only establishment.

places.name: Han Chin Pet Soo
places.text: A painstakingly restored Hakka Miners' Club that documents the activities of tin miners far away from home with cash to spend.

places.name: Kinta Riverfront Walk
places.text: Come here at night, as trees are beautifully lighted up, making it a romantic riverside walk. There's a small hut with an interesting exhibit depicting the rise and fall of Ipoh's tin mining industry.

places.name: Little India
places.text: Various Indian related outlets, including clothing and food. And you can also find Indian restaurants and cafes here. Every year the Deepavali Carnival is held by locals here.

places.name: Mural Art’s Lane
places.text: Mural Art’s Lane lies in Ipoh New Town where all the murals were painted on the back walls of old heritage houses. In an attempt to preserve them, Eric Lai, a local art teacher, started the painting of numerous murals on those buildings.

places.name: Perak Tong
places.text: Houses over 40 Buddha statues and many murals. There is a steep, tall staircase in the interior of the cave rising up to the top of its hill, where one is greeted by a beautiful and panoramic view of Ipoh and its surroundings.

places.name: Sam Poh Tong
places.text: Actually a cluster of three Chinese temples in Gunung Rapat. The first temple, Ling Sen Tong is shrouded in the smokey haze of hundreds of joss sticks.

places.name: Kek Lok Tong
places.text: Calm Chinese cave temple with good views on the other side of the same limestone hill as Sam Poh Tong. Being newer and a little richer than the other cave temples, the place feels much airier and cleaner.

places.name: Sri Maha Mariamman Temple
places.text: An old Tamil temple. Not only is it religious in nature but also a place for discourses, and on Sundays, children are given an introduction to verses in Tamil.

places.name: Kellie's Castle
places.text: The deserted mansion of an eccentric Scottish planter, located in Batu Gajah, is half an hour's drive from Ipoh city centre. Its main appeal lies in the belief that it is haunted and that secret passages leading to hidden chambers exist.

places.name: Tanjung Tualang Tin Dredge Ship
places.text: The last tin dredge that has not been dismantled from its old workspace is an example of how easy it was to extract alluvial deposits from the river by merely scooping up tin-bearing soil on an industrial scale and filtering out the ore.
places.address: 9th Km, Jalan Tanjung Tualang, Batu Gajah

places.name: Papan
places.text: A century-old half-deserted mining town built on a rich deposit of tin that was due to be dug up before the price of the metallic ore halved in the 1980s.

places.name: Royal Ipoh Club
places.text: Founded in 1895, this is the club's football and cricket ground.

places.name: Caving at Gua Tempurung
places.text: Gua Tempurung is the largest limestone cave in Peninsular Malaysia. Located close to the North South Highway's Gopeng Exit, it provides the opportunity to explore in detail the insides of a limestone cave.

places.name: Bukit Kledang
places.text: Trek up one of the many trails up the Menglembu-Kledang Hills (these are the hills you can see to the west of Ipoh with the radio-TV masts on the top) to enjoy the awe-inspiring view of the limestone outcrops that surround Ipoh.

places.name: Ulu Geroh
places.text: Be an ecotourist and experience the rainforest here. This is an Orang Asli kampung about one hour's drive into the hills east of Gopeng.

places.name: The Lost World of Tambun
places.text: Ipoh's only water theme park provides great rides and entertainment for families and also organizes tours into the nearby limestone caves for those interested in eco-tourism.

places.name: Gunung Lang
places.text: A general recreational park with a man-made waterfall and a long waterfront boardwalk. The serene 80-foot-deep lake, like many others in the region, hides the deep scars tin mining made on the landscape.

places.name: Golf
places.text: The Perak Royal Golf Club is the oldest of the golf courses located close to the city centre but there are also great golf courses at Clearwater Sanctuary in Batu Gajah and Meru Valley in Jelapang.

places.name: Seng Kee Food Trading
places.text: Still making heong pang in the traditional manner in the backyard of their house, and worth a look just to see the masters at work.

places.name: Yee Hup
places.text: The family-operated business started at home in the 1980s, before becoming a corporate company pumping out biscuits by the truckload from industrial sized electric ovens.

places.name: Hong Kee Confectionery
places.text: Family business famous for their Cantonese-style egg tarts. Come early as possible to avoid disappointments.

places.name: Chin Pomelo Farm
places.text: There are two types of pomelo to try, sweet (pale cream flesh) or sour (pink flesh). They vary on ripeness, depending on whether they're meant to be eaten fresh or for prayers.

places.name: Memory Lane
places.text: A flea market along Jalan Lim Bo Seng that takes places every Sunday morning. It is a good place to find imitation goods, antiques and other interesting local souvenirs.

places.name: Gerbang Malam
places.text: A popular night market among locals . Sells mainly shoes and clothes. Great imitations of backpacks, glasses and watches can be found as well...

places.name: Sin Meng Kee Products
places.text: Excellent Chinese vegetarian restaurant, there for more than 50 years. Very large options of food, mostly rice with toppings. Amazing mock meat and mushrooms.
places.address: Jalan Datuk Onn Jafar 34 (corner with Jalan Foo Choo Choon)

places.name: Choy Kee Bakery
places.text: A little out of the way for most tourists, retaining their authenticity. They sell Chinese breakfast pastries like prawn fritters, pork buns. They are best known for their flaky custard egg tarts.

places.name: Dai Shu Geok
places.text: Sells a variety of noodles accompanied by a large selection of yong tau foo, vegetables stuffed with fish paste. Soup base is also variable, from the normal clear chicken soup to the lemak coconut-based curry soup.

places.name: Restoran Li Heng Fatt
places.text: Bouncy fishballs, springy fish cakes and chewy fish paste dumplings, all served in a light soup with noodles of your choice, altogether better known as hor hee.

places.name: Restoran Nam Chau
places.text: Their dry curry noodles are topped with roast pork, chicken, prawns and a generous dousing of rich curry gravy. Twist a little lime into it, and the mix of spicy, sour, sweet and savoury makes the dish irresistible.

places.name: Restoran Kong Heng
places.text: Classic Chinese coffee shop with a variety of hawkers. They're noted best for their Ipoh kai see hor fun. The popiah (spring roll) is made fresh on the spot to order.

places.name: Restoran Thean Chun
places.text: Also known as the "hall of mirrors" for the large mirrors adorning the walls of the coffee shop, it is famous for its pork satay and Ipoh kai see hor fun. Their caramel egg custard is a perennial favourite, and can sometimes sell out by noon on weekends.

places.name: Tong Sui Kai
places.text: Long stretch of about 50 inexpensive hawker stalls selling mainly dessert but also a variety of Malaysian food. Best for dessert with a large selection of stalls selling Rojak, Ais Kacang and local speciality mixed fruits.

places.name: Kafe Best Hillview
places.text: Popular spot for dinner with a dozen of stalls serving local food. Can be difficult to find a seat and is a bit of a windy spot. Prices run a bit high for street food

places.name: Medan Aneka Selera/Gourmet Square
places.text: Variety is the name of the game here. A giant food court with hawkers selling just about every local fare imaginable as well as local renditions of Japanese, Thai and Western fare.

places.name: Family Food Court
places.text: A food court selling a variety of local dishes as well as some localized versions of Japanese, Vietnamese, Western and Thai cuisine.

places.name: Nasi Kandar Yong Suan
places.text: Nicknamed "Nasi Ganja" for the addictive quality of their food that keeps people coming back for more.

places.name: Restoran Samy
places.text: South Indian style banana leaf rice, the choices of curry are aplenty. Besides the typical chicken, fish, prawn, squid and mutton curries, they also serve crab, shark and seasonally, turkey curry as well.

places.name: Aun Kheng Lim
places.text: The red-and-white striped corner shop is the place for local speciality salt-baked chicken. Tender meat falls off the bone, just about enough to share for two or for one very hungry person.

places.name: Cowan Street Ayam Tauge & Koitiau
places.text: Less famous than Lou Wong and Onn Kee, yet far more popular among locals. Their opening hours are actually more variable than listed, but it doesn't stop hungry patrons from turning up and hoping to fill their cravings.

places.name: Restoran Tauge Ayam Lou Wong
places.text: Claims to be Ipoh's most famous purveyor of nga choy kai, the local speciality chicken and beansprouts. It's almost always a crowd here.

places.name: Ong Kee Restaurant
places.text: Onn Kee and Lou Wong have a much touted rivalry, having had stalls opposite each other for as long as locals can remember. Their quality is a little more consistent compared to the other place.

places.name: Michelangelo'S Pizzeria
places.text: Opened by an American, this place serves authentic American style pizzas in a lively rock-and-roll environment. Their wood-fired pizzas are crispy and toppings are very generous.

places.name: Foh San Restaurant
places.text: Most well established dim sum restaurant in the city. Tourists flock here by the bus loads (literally). Even with two floors, weekends have the place filled to the brim, with strangers sitting next to strangers as long as there's an open seat.

places.name: Ming Court Hong Kong Dim Sum
places.text: Many locals will argue that the dim sum here is superior to the more well known Foh San though their servings portions are also smaller. Their tong sui (sweet dessert drinks) are just as popular.

places.name: Restoran Yoke Fook Moon
places.text: The lesser known Dim Sum restaurant on "Dim Sum Street", one can generally avoid the crowds here. The char siew baos are freshly steamed and fluffy. Portions are slightly bigger and unlike Foh San and Ming Court, this place is open for dinner too.

places.name: Mun Choong Restaurant
places.text: The popular choice for special family occasions in Ipoh because of their consistently good food and large portions. Their steamed freshwater prawns with ginger are a crowd favourite.

places.name: Sun Swee Kiong
places.text: The place stands out with its large aquariums teeming with soon-to-be dinner. Kon chin har, pan-fried prawns to be dipped in soya sauce, is the dish you'll see on everybody's table.

places.name: Citrus Wine & Dine
places.text: Modern European fine-dining cuisine with Asian flair in a cosy atmospheric shophouse. Service is excellent with a selection of wines and cocktails. Offers cheaper 3-course set lunches during weekdays.

places.name: Indulgence Restaurant and Living
places.text: Serves European inspired meals all day. Opened by nationally renowned chef Julie Song, what was once a quaint cafe has now expanded to a laidback Western dining experience few can rival.

places.name: Funny Mountain Soybean and Traditional Tau Fu Fah
places.text: A little stall that serves creamy soy milk and tau fu fah (silky soybean curd in sugar syrup). They will serve you curbside, so you don't even have to get out of your car.

places.name: Nam Heong Coffee Shop
places.text: This Chinese coffee shop is the home of the famous "Ipoh White Coffee" and has links to the big OldTown coffee chain too. The egg tarts are fresh out of the oven, all sweet and flaky.

places.name: Sin Yoon Loong Coffee Shop
places.text: Located across the street from Nam Heong Coffee Shop, they are rivals in the "White Coffee" business. A favoured breakfast location among locals, they also serve good kaya cakes, which are sponge cakes with coconut jam.

places.name: OldTown White Coffee
places.text: Chain of coffee shops selling Ipoh's very own white coffee in comfortable surroundings. The first outlet actually began in Ipoh Garden South. Reasonably priced but uninspiring snacks.

places.name: Bricks and Barrels
places.text: A self-fashioned gastrobar, the place is a good place for families to dine during evenings in the quieter restaurant section before the nightbirds come in to chill around the open alfresco area.

places.name: Miners' Arms Bistro
places.text: Mock Tudor pub complete with wonky stained wooden beams and correctly placed apostrophe. The convivial clientele is entirely ethnic Chinese but the inevitable karaoke is kept at a civilized volume.

stays.name: Abby By The River
stays.text: Right next to the bridge on the Kinta River and can be spotted by its brightly coloured facade. A little bare, but rooms are fairly new and serviceable.

stays.name: D Eastern Hotel
stays.text: Refurbished rooms are basic albeit spacious. Traffic can get pretty noisy from the main road since the soundproofing isn't great.

stays.name: Grand Park Hotel
stays.text: A centrally located, nostalgic Chinese family mansion. Original Chinese decor is reflected in the connecting upstairs patio, the foyer and the large upstairs double rooms to the front of the building.

stays.name: Hotel Ipoh City
stays.text: Furniture is old but rooms and bathrooms are clean. Breakfast can be had in the hotel's Chinese restaurant.

stays.name: YMCA Ipoh
stays.text: Has two dormitories, one with ten beds and another with five, as well as smaller private rooms. Air-con not guaranteed.

stays.name: City Hostel Ipoh

stays.name: Hotel Excelsior
stays.text: Rooms are not very soundproof. Stay at the high floors for the best views. The Oversea restaurant is opposite.

stays.name: M Boutique Hotel

stays.name: MH Hotels Ipoh
stays.text: The hotel has concept theme floors and spacious deluxe rooms and suites. It has privileged check-ins and also a special floor for ladies.

stays.name: Regalodge Hotel Ipoh
stays.text: Provides free mineral water, soft drinks and instant cup noodles in their rooms. Also houses a foot reflexology centre and a fairly good fine dining restaurant called The Limestone's.

stays.name: Ritz Garden
stays.text: Deluxe and standard rooms are old and not in the best of condition. Has a private cinema, gym, swimming pool, computer and reading room, billiard table for all staying guests - no extra charge.

stays.name: Sekeping Kong Heng
stays.text: Restored bunch of heritage shophouses that is now home to a boutique hotel. The design is historically and architecturally interesting, leaning on the rustic side.

stays.name: The Banjaran Hotsprings Retreat
stays.text: This five-star wellness and spa resort has 25 luxury villas and is located in a 56-acre valley that is surrounded by a cluster of towering limestone hills with natural caves, waterfalls and geothermal hot springs, all unblemished by time.

stays.name: Happy 8 Retreat @ Old Town
stays.text: A terrace corner house converted into a boutique hotel, with the size and lighting that entails although the rooms are all very unique.

stays.name: Indulgence Living
stays.text: A boutique hotel with 3 designer suites and 4 themed rooms. The airy colonial bungalow lends an opulent yet homey atmosphere.

stays.name: Lost World Hotel
stays.text: A night's stay includes breakfast and access to the Tambun Hot Springs Spa.

stays.name: WEIL Hotel
stays.text: Room design is modern, stylish and clean. The rooftop swimming pool is a big draw, and there's a bar too, with welcome drinks on check-in.

destinations.name: Kuala Kangsar
destinations.intro: Kuala Kangsar is the royal town of Perak. It is the main town in the administrative district of Kuala Kangsar. It sits at the downstream of Kangsar River where it joins the Perak River.
destinations.eat_notes: Laksa while available in many parts of Malaysia, with slight variations, one unique feature of the Kuala Kangsar Laksa is the Laksa (the vermicelli, or "meehoon") itself. Almost all the Laksa vendors here serve their "laksa vermicelli" freshly made.

places.name: Ubudiah Mosque
places.text: The beautiful Ubudiah mosque was designed by Arthur Benison Hubback, a government architect who is notably credited for the design of the Ipoh railway station and the Kuala Lumpur railway station.

places.name: Sultan Azlan Shah Gallery
places.text: This is a gallery where records and artifacts of the present Sultan, who was also the 9th King of Malaysia, Chief Justice, and an avid hockey player who is also the Vice President of International Hockey federation is kept and exhibited.
places.address: galeri Sultan Azlan Shah, Bukit Chandan

places.name: Istana Kenangan
places.text: This used to be a royal palace. The museum is closed for renovation and the building cannot be accessed. It is still worth to look at the house from outside though.

places.name: Istana Iskandariah
places.text: The Sultan's Palace, Istana Iskandariah is another legacy of British architect serving in the then Malaya. It is a massive marble structure with a series of towers, topped by golden onion domes set among trees and rolling lawns.

places.name: Malay College Kuala Kangsar
places.text: One of the premier schools in Malaysia. It is now a full boarding school. It was founded by 4 sultans from the Negeri-negeri Melayu Bersekutu in 1905, as result of their desire to spearhead the future of Malays.

places.name: Sultan Abdul Jalil Shah Bridge
places.text: Connects the town of Kuala Kangsar to Sayong where village craftsmen produce the Labu Sayong.

places.name: Kuala Kangsar Clock Tower
places.text: Right in the middle of the town, which serves as the round-about for traffic management.

places.name: Labu Sayong
places.text: Traditional water pitcher (containers) for storing drinking water are a cottage industry in Kampong Sayong. Interestingly, these water containers provide natural referigeration and the water stored are cold when kept overnight in the container.

places.name: Kuala Kangsar Railway Station
places.text: A historical and interesting place to visit in this small Royal town. Not many railway stations this old exist in Malaysia these days. The station lies between Pandang Rengas and Sungai Siput.

places.name: Oldest rubber tree in Malaysia
places.text: The first rubber tree was planted in 1877 near the Kuala Kangsar District Office. There were nine trees planted and this was the only one which survived.

places.name: Ulu Kenas Waterfall
places.text: Have a family picnic at this waterfall which is in the Ulu Kenas Forest Reserve. Facilities available are basic, and only on weekends the stalls selling food items and snacks are opened.

places.name: Try the local speciality: Laksa
places.text: Plenty of stalls and restaurants can be found right next to the jetty.

places.name: Ferry ride
places.text: Take a ferry ride across Perak River in the passenger ferry boats plying very frequently between the town and Kampong Sayong Tebing. You get a 10-minute ride on the ferry to experience the local lifestyle.

destinations.intro: Pangkor Island is in Perak, on the west coast of peninsular Malaysia, about 100 km west of Ipoh and halfway between Kuala Lumpur and Penang.
destinations.eat_notes: No Problem - newly opened beach café and restaurant at Coral Bay, with in walking distance from Nipah Beach. Friendly staff and good chef, seafood, western and local food.
