destinations.name: Kota Kinabalu
destinations.intro: Kota Kinabalu is the capital of Sabah on the island of Borneo, often referred to by locals as just KK. This Malaysian city is a growing resort destination due to its proximity to tropical islands, sandy beaches, lush rainforest and Mount Kinabalu. KK is one of the smallest districts in Sabah but has the largest population and is the largest city in the state.
destinations.eat_notes: Kota Kinabalu is a cultural melting pot. Here Chinese meet Malays and Bruneis, Javanese, Filipinos and even a couple of Europeans, all of whom have brought along their own cuisine. Try out the many specialties offered at the various kedai kopi (often in buffet form making it easy to order) and shun fast food chains.

notes.title: School holidays
notes.text: Late May to June and most of December are school holidays: book early, and expect traffic and queues at anything family-friendly.

notes.title: Hari Raya Aidilfitri
notes.text: The biggest holiday of the year. Cities empty out, highways jam with people heading home, and many eateries close for the first few days. The date moves about 11 days earlier every year.

notes.title: Pesta Kaamatan
notes.text: Sabah's harvest festival, all May and peaking on 30-31 May: rice wine, traditional dress and the Unduk Ngadau pageant.

places.name: Atkinson Tower
places.text: Built in 1902 in memory of Francis George Atkinson, the first district officer of Jesselton, as Kota Kinabalu was then called. He died of a tropical disease in the same year at the young age of only 28.
places.address: on a hill beside Jalan Tunku Abdul Rahman, a few min away from the city centre

places.name: Signal Hill Observatory
places.text: Offers a good view of the city centre. There is a small drinks shop, it can be very busy as can the public road as it approaches sunset (around 6PM depending on the time of year).
places.address: 15 min walk up hill from the Atkinson Clock Tower

places.name: City Park
places.text: A small park and the only park in the city center opposite the court complex. It contains the British North Borneo Memorial which commemorates the soldiers who fought and died defending the British Empire during World War I.

places.name: Chinatown
places.text: Located in the city centre surrounding Gaya Street and Pantai (Beach) Street. There is a Sunday market here the Market starts early 6:30AM-1PM, arrive late you will miss it.

places.name: Sembulan Riverfront
places.text: Tiny pedestrian strip running along the river. Partly abandoned and thus doubtfully a high destination.
places.address: around the confluence of Sembulan and Karamunsing Rivers behind Sadong Jaya

places.name: Double Six Monument
places.text: A memorial site on the location of the 1976 plane crash which killed the state chief minister Tun Fuad Stephens and other state cabinet members.

places.name: Sabah State Museum
places.text: Has 3 storeys of exhibits. A good place to understand the history of Kota Kinabalu and Sabah. The museum complex also features the Science and Technology Museum, Sabah Art Gallery, railway gallery and a heritage village.

places.name: Islamic Civilization Museum
places.text: Has a history of Islamic civilization in Sabah.

places.name: Sacred Heart Cathedral
places.text: Roman Catholic church. It is the seat of the Archdiocese of Kota Kinabalu and the cathedral is one of the largest in Sabah.

places.name: Sabah State Mosque
places.text: The second largest mosque in Sabah, able to hold up to 5,000 worshippers. Designed an Italian architect, its dome and minaret is decorated with real gold.

places.name: Gurdwara Sahib Sikh Temple
places.text: The only Sikh Gurdwara in Kota Kinabalu. To enter you’ll need to cover your head, either with a hat, or a headscarf from one of the friendly volunteers at the temple.

places.name: Perdana Park
places.text: An park in Tanjung Aru featuring a light and musical water fountain, greenery, children's playground and jogging tracks. The park was built on the land formerly known as Hone Place where British government quarters stood.

places.name: Tanjung Aru Beach
places.text: A 20-minute drive from the city centre is the most popular public beach in the city.

places.name: Petagas War Memorial
places.text: Dedicated to the 176 members of the Kinabalu Guerrillas who attacked the Japanese occupying forces during World War II, in what was known as the "Double Tenth Revolt" (10/10/1943), who were subsequently detained and executed in Petagas.

places.name: Likas Bay promenade
places.text: A huge several kilometres promenade, used mostly by joggers and cyclists, that run along almost all the Likas bay. It starts about 1 km north from Jesselton point and runs up to the huge building of Malaysia Sabah University on the northern end of the bay.

places.name: Kota Kinabalu Wetland Centre
places.text: A 24-hectare mangrove conservation area used for recreation, education and research. It is located in Likas along Jalan Bukit Bendera Upper just 5 minutes drive from city centre (15 minutes walk from Signal Hill Observatory).

places.name: Kota Kinabalu City Mosque
places.text: This 'floating' mosque overlooking Likas Bay is the largest mosque in the city with interesting contemporary Islamic architecture. As of June 2018, the mosque's chairman is not allowing public transport to bring tourists to the mosque compound.

places.name: Che Sui Khor Chinese Temple
places.text: Contains an interesting 12-tier pagoda and is part of the Moral Uplifting Society.

places.name: Tun Fuad Park
places.text: Where the city meets the hilly jungles of Crocker Range. The park has 2 restaurants, hawker centers, the Water World theme park, a lake and jogging track.
places.address: on the eastern edge of the city, 15 minutes drive from city center

places.name: Tzer Ying Buddhist Temple
places.text: A pure Buddhist temple with adjacent Tzer Ying Buddhism Research Society.
places.address: Kampung Minintod Off Jalan Kolam-Minintod, 88200, Penampang

places.name: Tunku Abdul Rahman Marine Park
places.text: A collection of 5 islands (Gaya, Manukan, Sapi, Sulug and Mamutik) just off the coast of KK city.

places.name: Mari Mari Cultural Village
places.text: Showcases the historic culture, lifestyle, and homes of some of the 32 indigenous groups of Sabah.
places.hours: Sessions start at 10AM and 2PM. From January 2018 they only run the 6PM sessions
places.address: near the jungles in Kianson, Inanam about 25 minutes northwest of the city center

places.name: Kokol Hills
places.text: Offers a very nice view of Kota Kinabalu, the coasts and the sea from about 30 km away. The hills are pretty undeveloped but the road is good and new. As of January 2012, there is only one resort and restaurant called Kasih Sayang Resort.

places.name: St. Michael's Church
places.text: It was completed after 1945-1948 the large granite block were dragged to the site by buffalo and then dressed on site. It retains its old-style architecture.

places.name: Monsopiad Cultural Village
places.text: It's about a 30-miunite drive from KK city in the district of Panampang, near Lok Kawi Zoo.
places.address: Kampung Kuai Kandazon, Peti Surat 740 Malaysia, Penampang

places.name: Lok Kawi Wildlife Park
places.text: It features five female orangutans, Proboscis Monkeys, one female Gibbons, a Sumatran Rhinoceros, two tigers, local deer, various birds in a large aviary the Hornbills are impressive up close and in flight, eight elephants, and two sun bears.
places.address: near the small town of Lok Kawi

places.name: Tambalang Racecourse
places.text: Ahorse-racing track operated by Royal Sabah Turf Club in Tuaran.

places.name: Scuba Junkie KK
places.text: 5 Star Gold Palm IDC PADI Licensed Dive Operator.

places.name: Mr. K.K. Law
places.text: A budget-friendly option popular with the locals. The boat owner himself will be happy to come on the trip himself or help you arrange for more people to fill up the boat if your group doesn't have enough people.

places.name: Ultimate
places.text: Frisbee for all ages and abilities. Show up with enthausiasm and a basic knowledge of Ultimate rules and enjoy a game with the Ultimate players of Sabah.
places.address: Tu & Th: Pertama Pantai (1st Beach) Tanjung Aru district. Tanjung Aru Rugby Field

places.name: Filipino Market
places.text: Synonymous with pearls, local handicrafts, home decorations and lately crystals. Don't forget to bargain for good prices.

places.name: Sunday market
places.text: With everything from Malaysian delicacies, ground coffee, t-shirts, handicrafts, hardware to anything in between at bargain prices. A particular focus on clothing and jewelry.

places.text: Maybe think twice before going overboard on ordering some of the food items here due to the hygiene and smell, but this is an interesting wet market with a wide variety of fruit and seafood and other food selections.

places.name: IMAGO Shopping Mall

places.name: Wisma Merdeka
places.text: One of the oldest and smallest malls but still very popular. Ideal shopping centre for cheaper goods over five floors, at a fraction of the price of Suria Sabah shops.

places.name: Kompleks Karamunsing
places.text: An older but large mall that specializes in computers and electronics.

places.name: Centre Point Sabah
places.text: A large mall adjacent to Asia City, Api-Api, Warisan Square and Sinsuran. Easy parking within the centre with access to all floors.

places.name: Oceanus Mall

places.address: Jln. Tun Fuad Stephens Kota Kinabalu Sabah

places.name: Badben

places.name: Night Market

places.name: El Centro

places.name: Little Italy

places.name: Tavern Kitchen & Bar

places.address: Lot G-93, Imago Shopping Mall, KK Times Square Phase 2, Jalan Coastal

places.name: Gaya Vegetarian
places.text: Vegetarian Chinese restaurant with large portions, especially the soups.

places.name: Sunset Bar

places.name: Chocolate Factory

places.name: Bed

destinations.name: Sandakan
destinations.intro: Sandakan is a city of almost 440,000 people (2020) in Sabah, Borneo. It is the gateway to Sepilok Orangutan Sanctuary and the Labuk Bay Proboscis Monkey Sanctuary.
destinations.eat_notes: *Restoran Ajmeer Located at mile 3 (Hing Lee) and mile 4 (Bandar Prima). Specialize in South Indian food and Malay-styled fried food. Also serve lamb briyani, fish head curry, dosai, idli, vadai and other Indian traditional food.

places.name: St Michael and All Angels Cathedral

places.name: Agnes Keith House and Museum
places.text: Former home of author Agnes Newton Keith, now restored as a museum. Same ticket as the Sabah State Museum in Kota Kinabalu, so if you can cross Sabah in a day you can visit both for the price of one.

places.name: Gomantong Caves
places.text: The massive cave is home to swiftlets and their nests are harvested as a Chinese delicacy. The harvesting processes involves people climbing to the roof of the caves with bamboo poles and ladders.
places.address: The caves are 100 km by car from Sandakan, and there is little public transport.

places.name: Labuk Bay Proboscis Monkey Sanctuary

destinations.name: Semporna
destinations.intro: Semporna is a city on east coast of Sabah. It has a population of around 135,000. While there is not much to see and do in Semporna itself, it is frequently used as a gateway for diving and snorkeling trips to the nearby islands of Sipadan, Mabul, Kapalai, Mataking, Maiga and others.
destinations.eat_notes: It's easy to find stalls selling local delicacies like the following: Nasi kuning (yellow rice) — sold in the morning by the street — traditional breakfast for sabahan. It consists of rice, fish cook with chilli and vegetables. Good budget eating Pisang goreng (fried banana) — 10-20 cents each, sold by the street (same street with bakso and grilled chicken).

destinations.name: Klang
destinations.intro: Klang, also spelled Kelang, is the royal town of Selangor, on the west coast of peninsular Malaysia besides Shah Alam.
destinations.eat_notes: Klang is the original home of bak kut teh ("pork rib tea"), the Hokkien-style dish of pork ribs cooked in a strong, dark herbal stock, served with tea on the side. This is considered a breakfast dish here and family get-togethers on Sundays for bak kut teh are particularly popular.

destinations.name: Kuching
destinations.intro: Kuching is the capital of the state of Sarawak and the largest city in East Malaysia. Kuching is small enough to walk around but interesting enough to keep you there for several days, and a good base for exploring Sarawak.
destinations.eat_notes: Eating out is the major pastime, with a huge variety of eateries and food available. Most places are pretty cheap with excellent service but the more "local", the less English spoken. Be sure to sample some Sarawak laksa, but beware - it's considered a breakfast dish here and the popular places sell out fast.

notes.title: School holidays
notes.text: Late May to June and most of December are school holidays: book early, and expect traffic and queues at anything family-friendly.

notes.text: The biggest holiday of the year. Cities empty out, highways jam with people heading home, and many eateries close for the first few days. The date moves about 11 days earlier every year.

notes.title: Gawai Dayak
notes.text: The Dayak harvest festival on 1-2 June. Longhouses open their doors; towns go quiet as people head upriver.

notes.title: Rainforest World Music Festival
notes.text: Three days of music at the foot of Mount Santubong. Book rooms in Kuching well ahead.

places.name: Kuching City Mosque
places.text: Formerly the Sarawak State Mosque, Kuching's main mosque. Later it was re-designated as the Kuching Divisional Mosque. It was built in 1968 on a site that had been used for a wooden mosque as early as 1852.

places.name: Tua Pek Kong Temple
places.text: This temple is the oldest Chinese temple in Kuching and at the heart of the city. It was just at the opposite of Chinese Museum. It was built in 1843.
places.address: Jl. Padungan (East end of Main Bazaar)

places.name: Sarawak Museum
places.text: The Sarawak State Museum is the oldest museum in Borneo. It was established in 1888 and opened in 1891 in a purpose-built building in Kuching.

places.name: Kampung Budaya Sarawak
places.text: A living museum that spans 17 acres of land where you can experience the local culture and lifestyles of the various ethnic groups in Sarawak. The annual Rainforest World Music Festival happens each July.

places.name: Sarawak Textile Museum
places.text: yet another historical building on its own right
places.hours: Mon-Fri 8:30AM-4PM, Sat 8:30-12:30PM (closed Sundays and public holidays)
places.address: in the Pavilion, opposite the General Post Office

places.name: Fort Margherita
places.text: Completed in 1879, Fort Margherita resides at a breathtaking and strategic position at the riverside of Sarawak. It was once a defensive structure to protect Kuching from possible attack.

places.name: The Cat Museum
places.text: This is a large collection of cat memorabilia, since "Kuching" means "Cat" in Malay. The museum is at Kuching North City Hall at Petra Jaya, on top of Bukit Siol (Siol Hill).

places.text: In the Santubong rainforest you can go on a beautiful, sometimes strenuous and wet hike. Animals such as frogs, lizards and snakes are included. Entry is not possible after 10:00 for security reasons.

places.text: In an old traditional shophouse and almost resembles a typical indigenous kitchen but it is more modern and hygienic. The class includes a visit to the market where you will learn to choose and buy the best natural ingredients.

places.name: Lau Ya Keng Food Court

destinations.name: Bintulu
destinations.intro: Bintulu is a part coastal, part riverine town, and the capital of Bintulu District (7,220 km 2 ) in the Bintulu Division of Sarawak, Malaysia. It is a home to about 214,000 inhabitants (2020) in the area. Bintulu is known as a place of 'making a living'.
destinations.eat_notes: Be it budget or splurge, Bintulu is somehow a fine place for casual dining.

places.name: Council Negri Monument

destinations.eat_notes: For a fabulous gastronomical experience, Miri is the place to try out all sorts of food. Depending on your budget, there is a variety of eateries around. Chinese Hawker Center - Located in the hub of the city center next to the Chinese wet market.

destinations.name: Kuala Terengganu
destinations.intro: Kuala Terengganu is the administrative capital, royal capital and the main economic centre of Terengganu, on the east coast of peninsular Malaysia. The city is also the main gateway to many of the state's tourist destinations, including Kampung Cina, Pasar Besar Kedai Payang, Terengganu State Museum, and Batu Buruk Beach.
destinations.eat_notes: Keropok lekor, a kind of fish sausage served with sweet chili sauce, is a must-try. Many traditionally prepared Malay cakes (kuih) are sold in Kuala Terengganu - among other places, in the Pasar.

places.text: An Islamic-themed recreational park near the state museum. Models of famous mosques around the world are built here in smaller size. The famous 'Masjid Kristal' is also here.

places.name: Masjid Tengku Tengah Zaharah
places.text: This beautiful, simple white mosque built on the created lake flowing from the Ibai river attracts locals, especially in the late afternoon and weekends, for family activities.

places.name: Istana Maziah
places.text: A well known palace, standing strong at the foot of Bukit Puteri. One of few palaces owned by the Terengganu Royal Family, this beautiful palace is now used for royal occasions such as Royal Raya Open House or the installation of a new king.

places.name: Bukit Puteri
places.text: A hill fort behind the Bazar Warisan. It played a key role during the Terengganu civil war between competing sultans (1831-1876). The hilltop contains a bell, several keramat, a 'throne' and cannons facing the sea.

stays.name: Bubu Long Beach Resort
stays.text: This is the first ferroconcrete hotel on the islands, offering air-con, hot water and other creature comforts. Great views from the balcony.

stays.name: Symphony Chalet
stays.text: Well-worn wooden beach front huts (few more would see the beach if it weren't for a canopy they built) and larger stone huts for quite cheap.

stays.name: Keranji Beach Resort
stays.text: On its own quiet beach, a 20-minute stroll down a paved jungle path from the busy beaches. Simple wooden chalets with mosquito nets, and a place to eat.

stays.name: Alunan Resort
stays.text: Alunan is a 24-room boutique resort clambering up a steep hillside on Kecil's quiet south coast. All rooms are multilevel, with accommodation downstairs and a balcony/terrace upstairs.

stays.name: Perhentian Marriott Resort & Spa
stays.text: The first branded hotel on the islands. Three pools, three restaurants, dive centre, spa, and a price tag to match. Has its own deluxe ferry from Kuala Besut, with one return trip daily.

stays.name: Perhentian Island Resort
stays.text: This large resort is on Besar's nicest white sandy beach and equipped with the first swimming pool in town.

stays.name: Watercolours Paradise Resort
stays.text: Has clean but mostly basic non air-conditioned chalets (specifically request one if desired) with attached bathrooms.

stays.name: New Cocohut Chalet
stays.text: The staff is friendly and helpful. The restaurant offers basic meals and beer at regular prices. The beach in front of Cocohut has some corals which could make it hard to swim at the shallow ends.

stays.name: Tuna Bay Island Resort
stays.text: The seaside restaurant is also pleasant with fairly decent food and a small bar.

stays.name: Bubbles Dive Resort
stays.text: A very quiet and small resort. There is a restaurant and a good dive school. Friendly staff, Turtle and Reef Conservation Project.
